arxiv-2603-28001: Wang and nine co-authors present Varuna, a smarter way to recover RDMA links after a failure. Standard practice resends every in-flight request over the backup link, but some requests already ran, and resending them wastes bandwidth or breaks correctness. Varuna tags each operation with a small completion log, so after a failure it resends only the lost requests. Tests show it cuts recovery resend time by 65% with small steady-state cost.
arxiv-2603-28101: Zhang and seven co-authors present Heddle, a system that speeds up the rollout phase of agentic reinforcement learning. Rollouts stall because a few very long tool-using trajectories hold up the rest. Heddle schedules whole trajectories by predicted runtime, places them to cut interference, and shifts compute toward the long tail. It also migrates work during idle tool-call gaps. Across varied workloads, Heddle raised end-to-end rollout throughput by up to 2.5 times over top baselines.
arxiv-2603-28201: Jacobsen and three co-authors revisit perturbation methods for unconstrained bandit linear optimization. The classic trick adds random noise to a learner's choices. In the unconstrained case, they show the bandit problem collapses to plain online linear optimization. That link yields new expected-regret bounds, the first dynamic-regret bounds with the right path-length shape, and high-probability versions of both. They also prove the long-assumed square-root lower bound for adversarial linear bandits on a ball.
arxiv-2603-28501: Karagiannis and Symonds build transfer and norm maps for finite group schemes, where induction and restriction need not mirror each other. In the additive world, their transfer acts on modules and on Ext groups. Its surjectivity turns out to mark relative projectivity, a wider form of Higman's classic test. In the multiplicative world, their relative norm for algebras matches Mumford's norm for finite maps. On fields it reduces to a power of the usual norm.
arxiv-2603-28601: Dolliou and co-authors study small, impulsive bursts of extreme ultraviolet light along network loops on the quiet Sun. What powers these loops is still debated. They use six hours of data from Solar Orbiter and IRIS. They detect bursts in three loops and track four in detail. Some parts sweep along a loop at over 220 kilometres per second. Other parts start near a footpoint and move more slowly. Near one footpoint, they find small mixed-polarity field emergence. They suggest magnetic reconnection as a likely cause.
arxiv-2603-28801: Eng presents a sparse method to estimate local scaling exponents from short velocity profiles in turbulence. The records hold only about 40 points and are anchored at a boundary. The detector solves an l1-regularized regression over a mixed Müntz-Szász and Jacobi dictionary. Eng stresses that it is a finite-scale roughness diagnostic, not a pointwise Hölder exponent. On Johns Hopkins turbulence data, it reached an F1 score near 0.93 against longer-record labels. Higher vorticity linked consistently to smaller roughness exponents in conditioned samples.
arxiv-2603-28901: Oza and co-authors present a framework that helps mobile robots judge how to report hazards. A knife in a kitchen calls for a calm note, while the same knife in a corridor calls for an urgent alert. Their system uses vision and language models to assess criticality, time pressure, and mitigation options. It then adapts the message to the context. In over 60 runs with a patrolling robot, responses were faster than fixed priority baselines. User trust rose to 82 percent. Criticality checks improved both response speed and mitigation quality.
arxiv-2603-29001: Shah and Cortes present an algebraic framework for subspace pruning in Koopman operator work. Finite approximations rest on finding nearly invariant subspaces. Principal angles between a subspace and its image measure how close to invariant it is. Their framework uses principal vectors to cut subspaces and minimize that error. They prove it matches existing methods and can generalize more broadly. A rank-one update scheme tracks principal angles at far lower cost. Tests show the framework works in practice.
arxiv-2603-29101: Robinson and co-authors add computer vision to the Box and Block Test. Clinicians use this test to score hand and arm function after stroke. Standard scores miss how well a patient actually moves. Their system reads joint angles of fingers, arm, and trunk from plain video. It needs no depth sensors or calibration objects. They test it on 136 recordings from healthy people and stroke patients. The patterns separate healthy motion from stroke-related changes.
arxiv-2603-29301: Ma and co-authors adapt self-consistency to motion graphics made by language models. A prompt asks for a path, such as a circle spiraling. The model samples many candidate trajectories. Consistent ones are grouped by clustering. Two paths count as consistent if an allowed warp maps one to the other. Warps form families, from rigid to affine. An algorithm recovers the right family on its own. Generation accuracy rose by four to six percent. Verification precision beat vision-model baselines by 11 percent.
arxiv-2603-29501: Pleiss and co-authors present Target-Aligned Reinforcement Learning, a drop-in tweak for value-based methods. Such methods use target networks, lagged copies that steady training. Slow updates add stability but make learning signals stale. Fast updates do the reverse. Their method favors transitions where target and online estimates agree closely. That focus softens the harm of stale targets while keeping stability. Tests on discrete and continuous control benchmarks improved scores. Peak gains neared 38 percent, with little added run time.
arxiv-2603-29601: Mondal and co-authors define new measures of quantum connectivity for quantum networks. A network's worth lies in linking any two nodes with good entanglement. Physical topology alone does not capture that functional linking. Their quantum connectivity measure averages connection quality over node pairs. Two derived quantities capture the connected fraction and a node-level clustering score. All three depend on the entanglement protocol and network settings. Even a fully linked graph can fail quantum tasks, they show. That happens when edge concurrence drops below a threshold.
arxiv-2603-29801: Santini and co-authors release ENEIDE, a dataset for finding and linking named entities in old Italian texts. It holds 2,111 documents with over 8,000 entity notes. The texts come from scholarly editions of Leopardi's diary and Aldo Moro's full works. Notes cover people, places, groups, and literary works, tied to Wikidata where possible. It is the first public multi-domain set of its kind for historical Italian. Baseline tests show a wide gap between zero-shot and tuned models.
arxiv-2604-00001: Wang and team propose an optimizer-aware system for online gradient-based data selection and reweighting in fine-tuning. Gradient selection estimates sample utility, but existing methods target offline settings. The key idea views online selection as shaping the coming target-oriented update under current optimizer state. The team frames this as an update-matching problem, with subset construction accounting for links and redundancy. They then develop Filter-then-Weight, which filters useful candidates and optimizes their weights. Tests show it improves convergence and downstream performance over online baselines.
arxiv-2604-00101: Bertassi and four colleagues test whether active-galaxy light curves hide two massive black holes rather than one. They compare a single damped random walk against a pair of independent ones in a Bayesian analysis. Mock trials keep false alarms below 1 percent for both even and uneven sampling, though full parameter recovery stays modest. Pairs become identifiable when their noise timescales differ sharply, with a ratio below one fifth, while their variability amplitudes stay comparable, with a ratio above one fifth.
arxiv-2604-00201: Xuanyu Liang and five colleagues propose reinforcement-learning energy-saving methods for dense Open RAN base stations, controlling active and sleep modes for up to 6 radio units via near-real-time controllers. A federated version adds an aggregator app in non-real time with local agent apps, scaling across layouts of 6 to 24 radio units and regions 500 to 1000 meters. Federated TD3 converges up to 43.75 percent faster than centralized baselines, saves over 50 percent of network energy, and uses about 37 percent less training energy. Quality of service holds and policy robustness improves.
arxiv-2604-00701: Ma and colleagues propose Birdcast, a multicasting design for infrastructure-aided collaborative perception. Vehicle-to-infrastructure sensing uses a high node to send bird's-eye-view feature maps to cars, beating line-of-sight limits. But downlink sending creates a bandwidth squeeze. Cars also need mixed yet shared information fitted to their blind spots and places, making standard unicast and broadcast rules wasteful. Birdcast accounts for maps they want, posing feature choice and group sending as one joint problem to boost network utility under bandwidth limits.
arxiv-2604-00801: Liu and colleagues propose Routing-Free MoE, a mixture-of-experts design with no central router, Softmax, Top-K selection, or load balancing imposed from above. Each expert decides its own activation through continuous gradient flow. A unified adaptive framework balances expert and token loads through a tunable mix. Tests show the design beats baselines with better scale and robustness, offering lessons for future mixture-of-experts work.
arxiv-2604-00901: Li and Ramakrishnan propose HERA, a layered framework for multi-agent RAG. It jointly evolves teamwork and role-specific agent prompts, with global tuning of query-specific agent networks through reward-guided sampling and lessons learned. Locally, role-aware prompt evolution refines actions via credit assignment and dual-axis tuning. On six knowledge-intensive benchmarks, HERA beats recent baselines by an average of 38.69 percent while keeping robust transfer and token efficiency.
arxiv-2604-01601: Malu and colleagues study robustness of in-context fine-tuning, training a language model with labeled examples. What matters most is the choice of in-context examples against each target. Random contexts teach the model little from related examples even when present. Retrieved similar contexts hurt accuracy on targets without close neighbors and push label copying. Probes of weight-based learning, in-context learning, and copying link these failures to separate training dynamics. Contrasting how similar targets and contexts are within and across batches restores robustness.
arxiv-2604-02401: Kim and colleagues compare three backup based safety filters, Backup CBF, Model Predictive Shielding and gatekeeper, in one unified frame. Sharing a safety filter abstraction and notation, they expose common backup policy structure and key algorithmic differences. Comparison runs through filter inactive sets, where the nominal policy stays unchanged. Model Predictive Shielding proves a special case of gatekeeper, which relates to the interior of the Backup CBF inactive set. A key conservatism source emerges: safety is judged by backup maneuver feasibility rather than continued safe execution of the nominal policy.
arxiv-2604-02501: Khan and five colleagues survey ECG foundation models and medical language models for heart care delivered on wearable devices. Their central claim is that future heart-monitoring systems will act as agents, pairing signal-reading models trained on raw heart traces with language models that supply medical knowledge and reasoning. The review also covers shrinking models through quantization, pruning and distillation so they can run privately and efficiently on watches.
arxiv-2604-02601: Park and four colleagues offer WGFINNs, neural nets that learn the rules of motion from noisy data while obeying the laws of heat and energy. Older GENERIC-informed nets use a strong-form loss that fails under noise. The weak form tests the motion against trial functions instead, staying right on noisy data when those functions meet set conditions. Weighted losses also tame scale gaps across variables. The work is aimed at noisy lab data, where clean signals are rare.
arxiv-2604-02901: Berriot and four colleagues study energy conversion in tearing-driven magnetic reconnection in weakly collisional astrophysical plasmas. They use 2D hybrid particle-in-cell simulations on a Möbius-strip topology that doubles efficiency over regular conditions. Most of it happens in the nonlinear phase. Magnetic energy moves to ion kinetic energy in bulk outflows and to internal energy as heat, mainly inside islands. Ion temperature runs higher parallel than perpendicular to the field.
arxiv-2604-03001: Srinivasan, Gupta and Honnappa examine the variational form of nonlinear filters, which casts the filter as the lowest point of a free energy functional. That form needs absolute continuity between joint and product path measures. The team proves this condition fails whenever signal and readings share a common noise source. The two measures are mutually singular, so no reference can rescue it. They propose a conditional principle keeping noise correlations intact. It recovers Mitter-Newton for independent noises and gives a clear free energy rule for linear linked noise.
arxiv-2604-03101: Rather studies the zero-divisor graph of a truncated polynomial ring, where nonzero zero-divisors become vertices joined when their product is zero. He determines the spectrum of its A-alpha matrix, yielding the adjacency and signless Laplacian spectra as special cases. He further proves that the Laplacian eigenvalues and the distance eigenvalues of these graphs all come out integers.
arxiv-2604-03401: Platt and colleagues analyze classroom attention without storing identifiable video, using pose and gaze data only. Their single-GPU pipeline extracts skeletons with OpenPose and gaze with Gaze-LLE, deleting frames right after pose extraction and keeping only coordinates, which keeps the system FERPA-compliant. A reasoning model then gives zero-shot behavior analysis per lecture segment, shown through attention heatmaps and summaries.
arxiv-2604-03701: Shaoyang Cui and colleagues built VidNum, a checked set of 1,167 multiple-choice questions testing number reasoning in videos. Models must count, track, and combine quantities across frames, actions, and scene changes, with questions grouped into direct counting, conditioned counting, and compositional reasoning. The best model scored about 60 percent against about 98 percent for people, and structured counting proved a repeated weak spot.
arxiv-2604-04901: Liu and eight colleagues ground agent personalization in traces of file-system behavior, where coworker AI helpers still lack good training data. Privacy limits and the difficulty of collecting real traces block scalable study, while current methods focus on chats rather than file actions. Their FileGram framework simulates realistic workflows to generate fine-grained action sequences, and it adds a diagnostic benchmark for memory systems built on such traces. The goal is agents that learn work habits from what users actually do with files.
arxiv-2604-05401: Sun and Zhang study an elastic thin plate with dynamic boundary conditions on a domain with corners, where boundary kinks can sap solution smoothness. For domains whose corner angles stay small, they prove the system keeps polynomial decay under standard geometric control conditions. When wider corners cause sharper regularity loss, they show stability returns once feedback control is added at the corners.
arxiv-2604-05501: Dash, Narang, and Kumar reinterpret heat-capacity anomalies in disordered frustrated magnets, often read as signs of quantum spin liquids. Simulating a disordered spin-1/2 J1-J2 Heisenberg model on a square lattice, they identify a valence-bond glass ground state that melts into a glassy spin liquid when warmed. Its low-temperature heat anomaly comes from collective singlet excitations and ignores magnetic fields, giving a robust fingerprint for the glass phase.
arxiv-2604-05801: Tanabe and four colleagues advance CHRONOS, a cryogenic sub-hertz torsion-bar detector aiming at intermediate-mass black-hole mergers. Torsion bars, speed meters, and cryogenic mirrors target strain sensitivity near 10 to the power -18 per root hertz at 2 hertz. The team reports hardware overview plus commissioning of a Michelson interferometer prototype in Taiwan.
arxiv-2604-06101: Poorazad, Benzaïd, and Taleb's 2026 paper presents a privacy-preserving anomaly detector for the Industrial Internet of Things. Agents train models locally without sharing raw data, under federated learning. Homomorphic encryption shields sent model settings from model inversion attacks. A dynamic selection scheme sets its threshold from agent delays and data size, easing the straggler effect and traffic jams of old federated designs. It also avoids unfair selection under mixed IIoT data. The setup beats rivals on accuracy, precision, F1-scores, traffic costs, convergence, and fairness.
arxiv-2604-06201: Guo and eight colleagues test whether language models can read population-level patterns, not just single facts, with Text2DistBench. Built from real YouTube comments about movie and music figures, it hands models entity metadata plus comments. It asks distributional questions, such as estimating shares of positive and negative comments or naming the most and second-most frequent viewer topics. Its construction pipeline runs fully automated and keeps updating with newly emerging entities. Models beat random baselines by wide margins, yet performance swings widely across distribution types.
arxiv-2604-06401: Kommuru, Khanvilkar, and Parekh present ProofSketcher, a hybrid pipeline for reliable math and logic reasoning. Large language models often produce persuasive arguments with missteps: omitted side conditions, invalid inferences, or underivable lemmas. Such omissions are hard to spot, since flawed constructions can look mostly accurate. Theorem provers like Lean and Coq are rigorous through a small trusted kernel, but demand full formalization plus low-level detail. ProofSketcher splits the difference: a language model drafts a typed sketch in a compact language, and a lightweight kernel expands it into explicit obligations.
arxiv-2604-06601: Crowley and Larson show that sections of any line bundle on the augmented wonderful variety of a hyperplane arrangement form a coalgebra. These coalgebras match the power ideals of Ardila and Postnikov, which include zonotopal algebras as a special case. Proving cohomology vanishing on these spaces recovers many known results about zonotopal algebras. The authors also read the superspace versions of Rhoades, Tewari, and Wilson through bundle sections, proving their conjectured Hilbert-series formula for the central case. That closes a gap the authors had left open.
arxiv-2604-06701: Zhan and four colleagues fix a core flaw in tuned autoencoders: encoder non-injectivity. When distinct inputs collapse onto one latent point, warped stand-ins stall convergence, while rigid rules limit robustness. Their Bi-Lipschitz Autoencoder pairs an injective rule, built on a separation test to remove bad local minima, with a bi-Lipschitz loosening that preserves shape under drift. Setting out admissible rules with enough conditions, they show BLAE beats rival methods on keeping manifold shape while resisting sparse samples and shifting spreads.
arxiv-2604-06801: Garg, Mahapatra, and Sarkar study boundedness and compactness of composition operators on de Branges spaces. Starting from model spaces to Hardy Hilbert spaces in the upper half-plane, they examine composition operators on de Branges spaces of entire functions. Boundedness on a regular de Branges space forces the inducing symbol to be affine, while affine symbols under suitable conditions yield bounded operators. They further show that boundedness and compactness on general de Branges spaces differ from the Paley-Wiener case, marking a distinct behavior for this operator family.
arxiv-2604-07101: Wang, Pang, and Leckie present SurFITR, a large data set for spotting faked images in surveillance style scenes. Open image makers now let anyone fake visual proof, yet older fake data sets use full image fakes or large changed zones in object centred shots. Surveillance fakes are instead small, subtle, and set in varied views with tiny or half hidden subjects and poor image quality. SurFITR holds more than one hundred thirty seven thousand doctored images, made with a language model led pipeline across many scenes.
arxiv-2604-07201: Mounis and six colleagues address multimodal search, where a query mixing images and words must find plain-text documents. Their BRIDGE system first rewrites the noisy query into a compact search string with a reinforcement-trained aligner. A reasoning-tuned dense retriever then runs on that cleaned query. On a benchmark of 2803 queries across 29 domains, the full system beats vision-language encoders, and the aligner alone lifts a leading encoder past the best text-only retriever.
arxiv-2604-07401: Petrova, Polyachenko, and State study memory capacity in modern Hopfield nets with continuous states and geometric limits. They map phase boundaries for exponential capacity, testing Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels on sphere-bound neurons. Geometric entropy rests only on sphere geometry, not on kernel choice. Top capacity of one half arrives at zero temperature in the sharp-kernel case. Below that, one kernel keeps a critical line at all loads, while the other retrieves perfectly at any temperature under a load threshold.
arxiv-2604-07801: Dokme, Reichman, and Heck ask whether emotional wording alone can damage a language model's math reasoning. Their TEMPER framework rewrites problems in emotional styles while keeping every number and relationship intact. The resulting Temper-5400 set holds 5,400 verified pairs across three math benchmarks, tested on eighteen models. Emotional framing cuts accuracy by 2 to 10 percentage points. Stripping the emotion back out recovers most of the loss, showing the damage comes from style, not corrupted content.
arxiv-2604-08101: Tanboga proposes CWOT-CE, a Choquet integral-based analysis of composite endpoints in heart trials. These endpoints combine varied outcomes like mortality, nonfatal events, hospital stays, and biomarkers, yet standard methods lose information by targeting one dimension. Cox time-to-first-event ignores later data, Win Ratio discards tied pairs, and negative binomial regression treats death as plain censoring. CWOT-CE encodes six dimensions, survival, event-free time, AUC recurrent burden, last event time, marker, and alive status, joined through a non-additive fuzzy measure with pairwise links.
arxiv-2604-08501: Samsonau builds sciwrite-lint, a local citation checker for the age of AI assisted science writing. Running on one consumer graphics card with open models and public databases, it verifies that cited papers exist and match their claims. It also checks that cited papers are not retracted, and it traces one step into cited bibliographies. Tests on 30 unseen papers with injected errors show its value as a fast first pass for authors, journals, and reviewers, plus a proposed SciLint Score for citation chain integrity.
arxiv-2604-08601: He and Yu present OpenKedge, a protocol that governs how autonomous agents change system state instead of letting API calls mutate state at once. Actors submit declarative intent proposals, checked against system state, time signals, and policy before execution, then approved intents become contracts bounding actions, resources, and time under short lived identities. An intent to execution evidence chain cryptographically links each step, giving deterministic audit trails across multi agent and cloud tests.
arxiv-2604-08701: Zhang and five colleagues define a unified uncertain inference task across text, audio, and video, where models must give calibrated chance estimates for hypotheses from premises in any mix. Past work stayed in text or single modality yes no judgments, leaving no fine grained cross modality setup. Their human annotated set covers audio, visual, and audiovisual cases. Their CLUE method pairs teacher calibration with confidence probing, matching or beating zero shot models up to 32 billion parameters with a 3 billion parameter model.
arxiv-2604-08801: Gao and colleagues study what makes a task suited to prompt optimization, decomposing reward variance across system prompts into response variance and system prompt variance. Optimization succeeds when system prompt variance is large, but fails when response variance dominates. Adding more user prompts can hurt by shrinking system prompt variance, especially on mixed datasets. Their p1 method filters to a small subset of high variance user prompts, substantially improving optimization. Just two AIME 24 prompts yield a system prompt that generalizes across reasoning benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-09101: Jindal and three colleagues build CLIP-Inspector, a model-level checker for backdoors in prompt-tuned CLIP models. Groups with little data or compute often outsource training, with firms shaping models by prompt tuning. A rogue firm can follow the rules yet implant a backdoor forcing cued inputs into a foe's class. It rebuilds working triggers in a single epoch from only 1,000 out-of-distribution images. Tests across ten data sets and four attacks reach 94 percent hit rate, far above rivals, aiding vetting and repair for safe use.
arxiv-2604-09201: Zhao and twelve colleagues present CT-1, a vision-language-camera model that carries spatial reasoning into camera-controlled video generation. Earlier tools either steer cameras loosely from text or demand hand-set trajectory parameters. CT-1 estimates camera paths with vision-language modules and a diffusion transformer, using a wavelet-based loss to learn path distributions. Built on over 47 million frames, it improves camera control accuracy by 25.7 percent over prior methods.
arxiv-2604-09301: Chiplunkar and Pit-Claudel propose tracers for debugging and exploration, built from a program's full run record. Programmers understand unfamiliar or faulty software by guessing, then testing each guess, but tools aid testing far more than guessing. A step debugger shows only one frozen instant per pause, so programmers must piece together how state changed. The pair argue tracers should show code in execution order instead of source order. They weigh design options, early findings, and open problems.
arxiv-2604-09701: Neubauer, Rueckert, and Rauch propose PASTA, finding targets and anomalies from image-level labels alone. Industrial and farm perception demands real-time handling and pixel detail, yet full tagging is costly. Matching a scene with a nominal baseline, PASTA finds targets and anomalies in self-taught vision-transformer feature spaces. Text prompts guide zero-shot masking through Segment Anything Model 3. On steel-scrap and plant datasets, training time falls about 76 percent against domain baselines. Target masks reach about 88 percent intersection over union; anomaly masks, about 64 percent.
arxiv-2604-09901: Deheuvels and four co-authors study near-critical fields in eight Kepler red giants showing doublets and deviating gravity-mode periods. Three stars show partial suppression; the team adapts a non-perturbative rotation-style formalism to compute mixed-mode frequencies. Near-critical fields reveal the radial field profile, unlike weaker fields yielding only an average. Doublets fit m equals 0 and 1, not plus and minus 1, implying 100 to 700 kilogauss fields below the hydrogen-burning shell. Best-fit models have low masses, with fields likely arising in the main-sequence convective core.
arxiv-2604-10001: Kato and Yokoshi develop a nonlocal structured-light dichroism theory. Optical absorption is a bilinear functional of vector potential and current-response kernel, keeping vortex-beam structure. Circular, helical, and helical-circular dichroism act as distinct channels, projecting different parts of one response. The signal splits into symmetry, tensor, and angular sectors. Single-mode fields probe diagonal parts, while mixed modes reach off-diagonal coherence. Mixed-field polarization picks out scalar, axial-vector, and rank-2 tensor sectors. This yields selection rules for high-symmetry systems and low-symmetry diagnostics.
arxiv-2604-10101: Li and seven colleagues build ChangAn, a benchmark for telling human-written classical Chinese poetry from poems generated by language models, a hard task given strict meter, shared imagery, and flexible syntax. The set holds 30,664 poems, with 10,276 human-written and 20,388 produced by four popular models. A systematic test of 12 detectors across text lengths and generation strategies finds current Chinese detectors unreliable for this poetry, confirming the need for a dedicated benchmark.
arxiv-2604-10301: Allu and Kumar compute sharp second and third Hankel determinants for a convex subclass of analytic functions. They consider functions in the class C(phi), defined by a subordination condition with phi of z equal to one plus z over two, squared. The functions are normalized with value zero at zero and derivative one at zero in the unit disk. Sharp bounds for both determinants are the main results.
arxiv-2604-10501: Jha, Yelisetty, Sathya, and Sural build bespoke access control test data on demand. Past work polished policy methods yet left data making tools thin. Their MuSimA web tool spins synthetic ABAC sets from user picked value spreads. Users feed a JSON plan, or a short JSON plus hand drawn spread sketches read by a language model. Outputs download for scale tests across sizes and tangles, free for research use.
arxiv-2604-10801: Heck and Akrida present two polynomial-time approximations for sliding-window cover on stars. Each snapshot is a star whose center may change. In temporal vertex cover, each edge is covered by an endpoint, while sliding-window cover demands coverage each delta window. Temporal vertex cover is NP-complete on star graphs, but a fixed-parameter algorithm solves it. The new algorithms achieve delta-minus-1 and 2-delta-minus-1 ratios, exact for small delta. Tests show the methods beat the degree-based approximation in speed, even when window exceeds degree.
arxiv-2604-11301: Banerjee, Chakraborty, and Hoque build torsion elements in the class group of a number field from torsion in the Jacobian of a polygonal curve. Starting with n-torsion points on the Jacobian of an m-gonal curve, they produce n-torsion elements in the class group of a chosen number field K. The construction links curve torsion to class group divisibility, the theme of the paper's title.
arxiv-2604-11401: Zhang and four colleagues add CityGML urban meaning to Gaussian splatting scenes with GS4City. Two-pass raycasting of level-of-detail-3 models yields image-aligned masks. Parent-child relations validate and recover fine facade elements, and these geometry-grounded masks fuse with foundation-model predictions for consistent instances. Each Gaussian learns a compact identity encoding under 2D and 3D supervision. On TUM2TWIN and Gold Coast data, GS4City beats 2D-driven baselines by up to 15.8 IoU points on coarse building segmentation and 14.2 mean points on fine-grained semantics.
arxiv-2604-11601: Wu and seven colleagues present the MEGN model for fiber-optic links. The EGN model gauges interference power in fiber-optic links with independent symbols, where power depends on fixed stats: second, fourth, and sixth-order moments set by modulation and distribution. Coded modulation cuts interference by adding temporal correlations, breaking independence, with energy correlations matter most. MEGN extends EGN to account for energy correlations. Tested by simulations and experiments, it gauges mean interference power within 5 percent across rates and spans, giving a framework for tuning correlated modulation.
arxiv-2604-11701: Huang and four colleagues present HeartSway, a hands-on hammock capturing heart rate and tiny moves as traces for the next visitor. Human traces across city landscapes show everyday life and shared vibrancy in subtle poetic forms, and the paper explores biodata as stirring traces. A field study with 10 participants found HeartSway evokes connection, curiosity about prior users, and love for shared vitality. The work frames nameless archival biodata as design material for lived city traces, offering ideas for intimate asynchronous encounters between strangers and for reimagining public spaces.
arxiv-2604-11801: Yoon and seven colleagues present CLSGen, a fine-tuning method that lets a language model give sound odds for yes-or-no sorting tasks while still writing explanations. Plain discriminative tuning, they note, often wipes out explanation skill through catastrophic forgetting and linguistic collapse. On several test sets, CLSGen beats baselines on sorting scores, and its explanations match its predicted labels closely while staying easy to read.
arxiv-2604-11901: Liang and Caprioli simulate shear layers with hybrid models, kinetic ions plus fluid electrons, to study cosmic rays in supersonic flows. Starting from sinusoidal shear flows prone to Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, they watch turbulence develop and particles with large gyroradii ferry momentum between layers, creating a form of cosmic-ray viscosity. Even when cosmic rays hold little energy, raising their energy density boosts momentum transfer, provided their gyroradii stay below the shear length scale. They also track heating, ion acceleration, reacceleration, and magnetic growth.
arxiv-2604-12001: da Costa, Modenesi, Menezes, and Lopes propose Divergence-guided particle swarm tuning against early collapse around the global best. A tweak repels members near the global best, gated by a Gaussian kernel equal to a fast-falling KL-divergence function. On 36 benchmarks across sizes 10, 30, and 50, it beats standard tuning on multi-peak problems by 2 to 8 times. On single-peak terrains it hurts, adding one knob and 15 to 25 percent extra time with no long-run cost change.
arxiv-2604-12301: Agyemang and four colleagues measure seven tactics for cutting cloud language-model token use when a small local model triages work before a frontier cloud model. Local routing plus prompt compression saves 45 to 79 percent of cloud tokens on edit-heavy and explanation-heavy coding work, while the full tactic set with draft-review saves 51 percent on retrieval-heavy work. The best subset depends on workload, the study's most actionable finding for teams deploying coding agents.
arxiv-2604-12401: Zhijie Cai and five colleagues tackle federated fine-tuning of language models over wireless networks. Sharing full gradients costs heavy communication and memory, and gradients can leak private data. Their pAirZero framework pairs zeroth-order optimization with over-the-air computation. Devices then send only bit-level updates and need only inference-level memory. Transmit power and noise adapt to keep privacy steady across channel conditions. Tests show peak memory of just 25 percent on OPT-125M. Communication falls by orders of magnitude against conventional methods.
arxiv-2604-12701: Takehito Yokoyama proposes a mechanism for supercurrent-induced phonon angular momentum. Mixed parity and s-wave materials with spin-orbit coupling host the effect. Math yields formulas for the induced momentum. The paper explains what the effect means physically. The effect links flow, spin, and sound. Phonons are quanta of lattice vibration. Phonon spin thus joins charge flow and lattice shakes in these materials.
arxiv-2604-13001: Wang and 21 colleagues present XRZero-G0, a virtual-reality system for collecting demonstrations that teach robots dexterous hand skills. An ergonomic interface with a top-view camera and two specialized grippers feeds a closed loop of collection, inspection, training, and evaluation that keeps 85 percent of the data valid. Mixing a little real-robot data with larger robot-free data at a 10 to 1 ratio matches all-robot training while cutting collection costs twentyfold.
arxiv-2604-13101: Iyengar, Tiselska, Samaraweera, and Liu tackle a risk in aviation safety work: language models alone can invent facts and cannot show their sources. Their framework first uses language models to build and update an Aviation Safety Knowledge Graph from varied sources, then grounds answers in that graph through retrieval-augmented generation. The result beats language-model-only approaches on accuracy and traceability, supporting complex queries with verifiable, context-aware safety insight.
arxiv-2604-13201: Bentham and Srikumar present InfiniteScienceGym, a program-generated benchmark that tests whether language models can reason from lab data without carrying published-study bias or label noise. From a seed, the simulator builds, step by step, a closed repository with lifelike files and tabular data. A question maker produces answerable and unanswerable questions with exact ground truth. No model tops 50 percent accuracy overall, spotting questions with no answer stays a major weakness, and stronger models use tools better rather than merely using more tokens.
arxiv-2604-13301: Hasan proposes a honeypot protocol to catch AI models that behave differently when they think they are watched. The test varies only the system prompt across evaluation, fake deployment, and explicit no-monitoring conditions, holding task, environment, and scoring fixed. Running Claude Opus 4.6 in BashArena in honest and attack modes, he finds perfect task success and no side tasks in every condition, offering a baseline for future tests with stronger attacks and other models.
arxiv-2604-13601: Mata-Cervera, Guo, and Shen show that skyrmionic patterns in polarized light are fragile in a precise sense: an arbitrarily small disturbance that splits merged phase singularities can change the skyrmion number. For two superimposed vortex beams, the number generally follows the larger vortex charge, not the difference between charges, which holds only without disturbance. The finding matters for tightly focused polarization patterns and for beams passing through aberrations.
arxiv-2604-13701: Sahoo, Singh, and Sahoo study spin polarization of Lambda hyperons in hot quark-gluon matter. Lambda hyperons are short-lived particles made in heavy-ion collisions. Their spin can reveal how the hot matter rotates. Using second-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with medium vorticity, shear, and evolving magnetic fields, the team tracks thermal vorticity to the freeze-out surface. They separate vorticity and magnetic contributions to global polarization. ALICE lead-lead data at two energies agree in broad terms.
arxiv-2604-13901: Cárdenas, Silva, and Jiménez-Galán compare how strong light fields drive electron-hole motion in two single-layer materials, semiconducting MoS2 and metallic NbSe2. Electron interactions boost harmonic output strongly in MoS2 and shift its phases and emission angles, while NbSe2 shows a weaker boost with clear phase and angle changes. Carrier entry into empty NbSe2 bands follows a tunneling picture, giving field control over when and where carriers land.
arxiv-2604-14001: Naveriani and colleagues bring diffusion language models to speech recognition. They test masked and uniform-state variants to re-rank guesses. A new joint-decoding method merges CTC frame scores with uniform-state label scores at each step. It blends sound evidence with language knowledge. Both diffusion variants improve recognition a lot, and the team publishes code and guides.
arxiv-2604-14101: Ben-Maimon and colleagues study quantum light-matter links from two-layer atom arrays in free space. They allow layer spacing to depart from Bragg symmetry. Mapping the problem to one line shows efficiency follows from reflection and transmission. That gives an easy lab readout. Off-Bragg setups suppress diffraction losses by destructive interference. A shared dark state with spacing-tuned coupling allows a new quantum memory scheme.
arxiv-2604-14301: Bagchi and Mondal build Carrollian fermion actions by expanding a relativistic Dirac theory in powers of the speed of light. They then link light-cone fermions to Carrollian fermions in one fewer dimension. Their bridge joins three views: direct Carrollian constructions, the small-speed expansion, and light-cone motion. The work explains why Carrollian fermions in a given dimension share traits with relativistic fermions in that dimension and in one dimension higher.
arxiv-2604-14401: Lu, Crotty, and Çetintemel introduce Credo, a control layer for language-model pipelines that stores semantic state as beliefs and steers behavior with declarative policies over those beliefs. Imperative loops, fleeting memory, and prompt-buried logic make agent conduct opaque and brittle, so Credo instead routes execution via a database-backed semantic control plane. Beliefs and policies then guide choices like model selection, retrieval, and corrective re-execution without touching pipeline code. A decision-control demo shows the design adapting as evidence arrives and earlier conclusions change.
arxiv-2604-14501: Zubić, Li, Wang, and Scaramuzza study how depth, precision, state size, and chain-of-thought affect multi-layer SSMs. For table function composition, they prove any L-layer model solving L-plus-three composition needs dimension squared times precision growing with size over layers cubed. Conversely, a K-plus-one-layer model with unit dimension and log precision solves K-composition exactly. Post-input reasoning cannot dodge the lower bound, while input-interleaved reasoning allows bidirectional streaming simulation. Width and precision trade off only then.
arxiv-2604-15001: Ping and seven others propose COEVO, unifying correctness and PPA in LLM-based RTL generation. Existing methods split correctness and PPA, delaying PPA until correctness, and discard promising partial candidates. COEVO treats correctness alongside area, delay, and power, with an enhanced testbench. An adaptive gate lets partial candidates guide search, and Pareto sorting keeps trade-offs without manual weights. On VerilogEval, COEVO reaches 97.5 percent Pass@1 with GPT-5.4-mini, beating baselines and attaining best PPA on 43 of 49 RTLLM designs.
arxiv-2604-15101: Gomez, Wang, and Fu design a ranking learner that is not tied to a single score. Current methods tune to one metric such as NDCG or MAP, which makes training rough and weakens transfer to other scores. Their listwise framework pairs a smooth ranking approximation with a per-query squared-error loss, trained by gradient boosting. Tests show it beats current leaders on retrieval measures at similar speed.
arxiv-2604-15301: Jiang and three colleagues rethink gloss-free sign language translation, which converts signing video to text without an intermediate sign glossary. Signers build meaning on the fly from context, space, and movement, so the team inserts an ordered chain of latent thoughts between video and text. They then plan wording before grounding it in video evidence. Tests across benchmarks beat prior gloss-free methods, aided by a new large dataset.
arxiv-2604-15501: Baring and 28 colleagues refine hard X-ray polarization measures of the Crab pulsar and nebula from an extended XL-Calibur balloon flight. A new phase-recovery method rescues timing for about 95 percent of GPS-off data, using the pulsar's 33-millisecond period as an external clock. Nebular polarization lands near 28 percent at about 127 degrees, aligned with the spin axis, supporting synchrotron emission from the inner nebula.
arxiv-2604-15801: Boscagli and three colleagues use direct numerical simulations to test a passive way of calming hypersonic boundary layers: streaks created by varying surface temperature across the span. Across Mach numbers from 4.8 to 6, the steady streaks cut the energy of the second Mack mode, a planar instability that drives transition to turbulence, by up to about 60 percent. For a Mach 6 case, the best streak spacing runs roughly 8 to 10 times the local boundary layer thickness.
arxiv-2604-16101: Jin and six colleagues propose quantum-resistant teleportation. They guard the classical correction channel with post-quantum codes against future quantum attackers. They show finite quantum memory links physical and code security. Its brief coherence time caps distance, limits tolerable code overhead, and bounds the attack window. Under realistic settings, secure range runs from 191 kilometres with one code to 199 kilometres with another. Attack odds peak then fall as decoherence wins.
arxiv-2604-16201: Behari and five colleagues present DENALI, a large real-world dataset for seeing around corners with cheap LiDAR sensors. Consumer LiDARs normally give one depth per pixel, yet internally record full time-resolved histograms whose multi-bounce returns carry hidden-object clues. DENALI holds 72,000 hidden-object scenes across shapes, positions, lighting, and resolutions, showing such sensors can support accurate data-driven perception of objects out of direct sight.
arxiv-2604-16401: Fan and colleagues note that most graph-based retrieval systems send every question to the same large generator, wasting money on easy queries. GraphRAG-Router instead routes each question hierarchically across different retrieval systems and generators. It warms up with supervised training, then refines choices through two-stage reinforcement learning with a cost-aware reward that grows harder over time. Across six question-answering benchmarks it beat leading baselines while cutting overuse of large models by nearly 30 percent, keeping strong performance on unfamiliar questions.
arxiv-2604-16601: Kreckel and colleagues verify what, and where, the Galactic Center Lobe is. Using optical spectra from SDSS-V, they confirm it as a foreground photoionized HII region, not tied to the center. A map with extinction shows ionized gas in an outer loop that leaves the interior empty. All diagnostics agree with photoionization, and gas kinematics show uniform velocity across the bubble. Comparing reddening with dust maps puts its distance at about 2 kiloparsecs. Its size and shape recall nearby Barnard's Loop, suggesting a distant young cluster lights the shell.
arxiv-2604-16701: Bärligea, Sims-Goh and Kottmann broaden Lie simulation beyond free-fermion settings. Lie-algebraic sim shows dynamics in an adjoint space sized by the ruling moving Lie algebra. It runs expectation values fast whenever that algebra grows slowly with system size. New groups of poly-size algebras plus symmetry-fit bases make prep doable. A Pauli orbit representation handles swap-proof motion, and a Gell-Mann picture handles Hamming-weight motion. Benchmarks confirm good preprocessing scaling and prove large-scale sims beyond state-vector reach.
arxiv-2604-17501: Xu and five colleagues blend two fixes for scarce human preference data in language-model alignment. CoAct uses self-consistency to sort machine-labeled examples into trustworthy ones and ones needing a human oracle. Oracle feedback then steers the model toward generating instructions it can actually solve. The mix beats pure self-rewarding on reliability and pure active learning on scale. Across three reasoning benchmarks and two model families, gains average 13.25 percent on GSM8K, 8.19 percent on MATH, and 13.16 percent on WebInstruct.
arxiv-2604-17701: Liu and six colleagues propose WISV, a radio-aware meaning check system for shared device-edge guess decoding. Guess reading improves resource use across varied nodes, but token-level checks cause many rejects, shrinking runs and raising rounds under shifting states. WISV moves beyond token matching with a channel-aware pass policy. It adds a light head to the edge LLM to judge guess tokens by mixing hidden codes with instant channel state info. Two plans, full-hidden upload and mismatch-first, balance check quality against cost.
arxiv-2604-17901: Yamaguchi and Harashita work out the reduced automorphism groups of small-genus hyperelliptic curves of 2-rank zero in characteristic 2. Such curves take the Artin-Schreier form. The authors first clarify the semidirect-product structure of these groups for arbitrary genus. Full details for small genera then follow from work in Magma. From this work they state two conjectures, analogues for their curves of the Oort conjecture on generic supersingular abelian varieties.
arxiv-2604-18001: Silva-Rodríguez and Konukoglu propose an approach to make endoscopic super-resolution safer, since sharpened surgery videos risk hallucinated structures and added noise. A lightweight error predictor working on middle layers estimates pixel error with low latency. Those estimates become conformal failure masks, marking regions where the output should not be trusted. The method rests on conformal risk control, the method gives proven guarantees on error limits and missed failures, and tests on image and video super-resolution show it flags unreliable work.
arxiv-2604-18201: Sethi, Shah, Gandhe, and Nayak present DiffuSAM, a tool for finding described objects in remote-sensing images. It mixes diffusion-based location cues with top segmentation tools, RemoteSAM and SAM3, to tighten bounding boxes. The mix adapts across hard scenes by joining generative and segmentation strengths. Tests show accuracy up by over 14 percent at the Acc@0.5 mark versus the best prior methods.
arxiv-2604-18301: Van Buchem and five colleagues test how lava makeup shapes the light spectra of hot rocky exoplanets. Interpreting James Webb spectra demands linking silicate melt chemistry to the air above it. The authors vary oxide abundances in dry lava models, tracking vapor chemistry and heat structure. Titanium oxide in the melt drives titanium oxide gas, warming the surface and muddying heat-redistribution estimates. Silicon oxides grow stronger with melt silicon content, and shifts of about tenfold could show in 12 eclipse observations.
arxiv-2604-18401: Wang and eight colleagues propose CAPO, a critic-guided method for training language-model agents with reinforcement learning. Critic-free methods dominate, but critics suit long-horizon tasks by judging states and assigning credit. Standard critic methods work at token granularity, though environments change only after full actions. CAPO values states at action boundaries, assigns advantages to whole actions, and aggregates token ratios within actions with length calibration, beating representative methods on question-answering, paper search, and text-world tasks.
arxiv-2604-18601: Akbari and four colleagues analyze GRS 1915+105, a black hole binary whose heartbeat pulses come from radiant-pressure wobbles, phase by phase. Each cycle is divided into five phases using 24 Swift looks and AstroSat data. Narrow-band XRT fits show inner disk temperature and seeming radius linked. Broadband fits support a constant disk heat, while tying scaling is refused, leaving about 20 percent radius swing. XRT disk swings reflect a limited bandpass, where disk values absorb coronal variability. Diagrams show spectral loops, backing coronal change as the driver.
arxiv-2604-18801: Ren and four colleagues propose a correction technique that preserves single linkage cluster membership when particle data are compressed with bounded errors. Existing tools bound only point errors, yet small shifts near a linking threshold can split or merge whole clusters. The method works on outputs from standard tools and stores a compact edit stream, enforcing only the constraints needed to keep clusters intact. Tests on cosmology, molecular, and fluid data keep clusters intact while improving compression ratio by up to four times.
arxiv-2604-18901: Llorente-Saguer shows harmful intent is linearly separable in the residual streams of aligned models. A direction fitted from 100 labelled examples per class reaches a mean effective AUROC of 0.982 across 12 models from four families. It generalizes to three held-out harm benchmarks plus a hard benign control. The result holds even in abliterated variants with the refusal mechanism removed, where it nearly matches its instruction tuned counterpart. The author argues safety work should report low false positive rates, since AUROC alone hides large gaps there.
arxiv-2604-19101: Brynes and eleven colleagues implement auto-generating digital twins for particle accelerators. A virtual control system mirrors the hardware and updates a simulation model, which feeds results back into virtual diagnostics. All lattice information cascades from a single ground source of truth, removing naming ambiguity between simulation and hardware. The design is modular, letting researchers plug in their own models and lattices while keeping structural coherence. It has been tested at CLARA, the ISIS injector, and the proposed UK XFEL.
arxiv-2604-19201: Wang and nine colleagues split code editing into a cascade pairing a large model with a smaller one. Large models edit accurately but inefficiently, regenerating mostly unchanged files, while smaller models lack long-context capacity. First, the large model handles the harder sketch generation; then, the smaller model applies sketches to the code. The cascade cuts large tokens since output comes from the smaller model. Its effectiveness is limited by small models' weak long and cross-file handling.
arxiv-2604-20301: Crucinio and Pathiraja study sampling from a target law, framed as a search over laws that cuts Kullback-Leibler gap. They swap the fixed target for moving targets built by geometric tempering along Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao gradient flows. Convergence comes exponentially fast in continuous time, with new bounds in both cases, and popular time discretisations get the same treatment. In the Fisher-Rao case, mixing start and target laws by geometry never speeds convergence, in continuous or discrete time, and the work derives new adaptive tempering plans.
arxiv-2604-20401: Rathee and four colleagues present Onyx, a cost-efficient design for oblivious approximate nearest neighbor search over external SSDs. Trusted execution environments protect data on third-party machines, but queries leak through disk access patterns, and hiding those patterns with oblivious RAM is costly. Onyx flips the usual design, saving bandwidth at the search layer and access count at the oblivious RAM layer, where each choice fits better. Against the prior best oblivious system, Onyx cuts cost about two to ten times and latency about two to twelve times.
arxiv-2604-20601: Volovikova and four others offer SuperIgor, a method for following tasks that lets a language model make and refine high-level plans by itself. Unlike prior methods, it needs no preset subtasks, cutting manual labels. An RL agent learns to use the generated plans while the language model revises those plans from RL feedback and ratings, so agent and planner improve jointly. Tests in rich, random worlds show SuperIgor agents follow instructions more strictly than baselines and extend strongly to unseen tasks.
arxiv-2604-20701: Kawamata, Nakano, and Fujii propose a divide-and-conquer neural surrogate framework for quantum sampling to accelerate Markov chain Monte Carlo under Hamming weight constraints. The method splits Ising graphs into subgraphs and samples them via QAOA with an XY mixer. It trains neural surrogates on Hamming weight to provide proposal distributions for each subset, preserving the constraint. In Boltzmann sampling, the decay rate constant improved by factors of about 20 and about 8 over methods. Applied to an MNIST mask problem, it reached faster convergence and about 2 percent higher classification accuracy.
arxiv-2604-21001: Yuan, Du, Lee, and Palanisamy present VRSafe, a virtual-reality QWERTY keyboard built to resist keystroke inference, in which an attacker reconstructs passwords from typing motion. The keyboard plants false-positive keystrokes in the data an attacker collects, muddying the true password, and pairs this with a detector that spots logins attempted with inferred credentials. Simulation and a real-world user study show it sharply cuts inference accuracy at modest usability cost.
arxiv-2604-21101: Brooks Kinch and eight colleagues embed a transformer that predicts step by step inside a math scheme that preserves key structure, aiming for steady long-horizon forecasts of chaotic systems. The design provably keeps energy-like quantities intact and caps training gradients, so training cannot blow up. It beats current foundation models with 65 times fewer parameters, and a small fusion stand-in trained on just 12 runs is 9,000 times faster than particle-in-cell simulation.
arxiv-2604-21201: Ellis Buckminster studies universal circles, the boundary objects Thurston and Calegari-Dunfield introduced for foliations. Building on earlier work with Taylor, he studies branching Anosov foliations, which admit nonconjugate universal circles. He proves the leftmost such circle maps to the ideal 2-sphere by a Cannon-Thurston-type map on a hyperbolic manifold. This gives a new construction of such maps. As a corollary, the manifold's fundamental group acts on that circle with pseudo-Anosov dynamics.
arxiv-2604-21501: Mingyue Cheng and four colleagues present GeoMind, an agentic framework modeling rock-type classification from well logs as step-by-step reasoning rather than static mapping. Its seeing, reasoning, and checking modules turn logs into trends, infer rock-type guesses from varied evidence, and check predictions against rock-layer rules. A global planner adapts to inputs. Step supervision improves middle reasoning steps rather than final outcomes alone, keeping decision paths within geological rules. Tests on four well datasets show GeoMind beats strong baselines in classification, with clear, traceable decisions.
arxiv-2604-21601: Alexander Milner and Jack Shotton study the smallest invariant factor of points on an elliptic curve over the rationals. They ask when the constant giving the density of primes with a given factor stays positive. For curves without complex multiplication, they use the image of the adelic Galois representation to strengthen an earlier result by Kim. Positivity, they show, under the generalized Riemann hypothesis means infinitely many such primes exist. Experiments suggest the constant vanishes only when division fields coincide, and they document coincidence families from abelian division fields.
arxiv-2604-21701: Chatzittofi and three colleagues extend the theory of self-propelling particles to chiral active fluids, where odd viscosity breaks the usual rules of fluid mechanics. They derive speeds for spinning and drifting motion of a round swimmer with any activity and mobility pattern on its surface. Examples cover chemically active colloids with symmetric and asymmetric coatings. The results also apply to groups of such particles in fluids that break time-reversal and parity symmetry.
arxiv-2604-22101: Le Guay and seven colleagues build a bias-programmable gate from three nanocryotrons for on-chip photon coincidence detection. The gate selects AND, XOR, or OR functions and runs on two electrical pulses at about 4 K. Error rates stay below 10^-3, bias margins reach ±21.7 percent, and speeds extend to 25 MHz over narrower bias windows. It detects coincidence and odd parity from two detector outputs with error rates under four hundredths. As a proof of concept, the gates drive loads over 1 V, hinting at use with electro-optic modulators.
arxiv-2604-22201: Kellermann and six colleagues work out, from lattice quantum chromodynamics, the total rate for a Ds meson decay. The decay yields strange-flavoured particles plus a lepton. Their simulations use two light quark flavours plus a strange flavour. They extrapolate to real quark masses and continuous space-time, counting every possible final state. The result agrees with existing measurements, with error at the few-percent level.
arxiv-2604-22301: Tallavajhula and five colleagues demonstrate a thin-film aluminium nitride microbolometer, a heat sensor for very long-wave infrared light. The device hangs a 100-nm membrane above a platinum reflector across a 1-um air gap. Absorption peaks near a material vibration near 15 um and grows stronger with the suspension. A perforation pattern cuts thermal mass and boosts absorption with no further thinning. Response spans 14 to 18 um, peaking around 921 ppm/mW near 15 um. Such sensors could serve multispectral imaging, on-chip infrared spectroscopy and chemical sensing.
arxiv-2604-22401: Elias and seventeen colleagues measure quiescent fractions, the share of dead galaxies, in 16 groups at redshifts 1.6 to under four. They fit COSMOS2020 members' spectral energy distributions. Quiescent fractions hit about 50 percent in hot-accretion groups, zero in cold-accretion groups. In mature hot-accreting groups, massive quiescent galaxies cluster inside, with a more-than-four-sigma excess over the outskirts. Most groups lack a clear brightest member and show small mass gaps, signalling assembly. The results support cold-to-hot transition triggering quiescence, with environment beating internal processes.
arxiv-2604-22601: Erfan and three colleagues address AI-assisted problem-to-code generation with Dafny-based formal verification. Language models show promise in software work, yet correctness is undermined by erroneous or hallucinated code. Formal verification demands models build logic alongside specifications later proven correct by a verifier. The authors release NL2VC-60, 60 complex algorithmic problems. They test 11 problem sets across seven open-weight models with tiered prompting: contextless, signature, and self-healing prompts, the last using Dafny verifier feedback. To block trivial-specification cheating, they integrate uDebug for functional checks.
arxiv-2604-22701: Milović and Milošević extend Gel'fand integration, an integral for functions taking values in operator spaces, from Hilbert-space operators to certain Banach spaces. They give sufficient conditions for the integral to be (q, p)-summing and use the machinery to answer a question raised in earlier work. Applications to positive operator-valued functions between function spaces follow.
arxiv-2604-22901: Liu, Yu, and Wu propose E2-CRF, an error-feedback caching method that speeds frequency-domain diffusion models for time series generation. It exploits spectral localization, with energy concentrated at low frequencies, and mirror symmetry, which cuts the working frequency range in half. A closed-loop error-feedback system caches transformer features across steps, recomputing only high-energy or fast-changing tokens on event-driven triggers. The method reaches about 2.2 times speedup while preserving sample quality across five data sets.
arxiv-2604-23001: Wang and nine colleagues survey vision-language-action robotics, arguing that progress depends less on model architecture than on data engines and evaluation. The survey covers datasets, benchmarks, and data engines. For datasets it exposes a fidelity-cost trade-off capping large-scale collection. For benchmarks it finds gaps in compositional generalization and long-horizon reasoning. For data engines it finds shared limits in physical grounding and sim-to-real transfer. Four challenges emerge: aligned representations, multimodal supervision, reasoning tests, and data generation at scale.
arxiv-2604-23201: Kozlov and Leiderman examine graph compactifications of topological groups in detail, applying graph and Ellis methods to extend algebraic moves to them. Their accounts cover Roelcke, Ellis, WAP, and graph compactifications. Using split theorems of Arhangelskii, they show compactification accounts shed light on topological properties of remainders. Examples include subgroups of the permutation group under its usual topology and the symmetry group of a LOTS under pointwise limits.
arxiv-2604-23801: Buskila runs a controlled comparison of domain fine-tuning versus retrieval-augmented generation for medical multiple-choice answering at the 4-billion-parameter scale. Holding size, prompts, decoding, retrieval, and evaluation fixed, he tests both a general and a domain-tuned model with and without retrieved passages. Fine-tuning gains about 7 points over the general baseline, while retrieval adds no significant gain in either model, so knowledge in weights beats knowledge in context here.
arxiv-2604-24001: Yuan and six colleagues propose CT-FineBench, a benchmark that grades machine-written CT reports on fine clinical detail rather than surface word overlap. Built from CT-RATE and Merlin, it turns finding-specific attributes such as location, size, and margin into questions answered from each generated report. Tests show it tracks expert judgment more closely and catches small factual errors that coarser metrics miss.
arxiv-2604-24201: Fan and seven colleagues propose CMGL for cancer subtyping from multi-omics data. Modality usefulness and noise vary by cancer and patient. Most graph methods bury per-patient reliability in the classification goal, letting weak modalities dilute fusion and noisy omics corrupt propagation. CMGL estimates modality confidence via evidential learning, freezes them during fusion, and uses a separate consistency graph. It beats rivals by about 4 percent on four single-cancer tasks, recovers breast PAM50 subtypes, and transfers without fine-tuning to kidney cancer, splitting patients into prognostic groups.
arxiv-2604-24401: Foo and four colleagues test whether audio benchmarks truly measure hearing. High scores may not reflect true hearing: a model answering without sound breaks the benchmark. Their diagnostic uses two axes: text prior, answerability from text alone, and audio reliance, real dependence on sound. Across eight models and three benchmarks, models keep 60 to 72 percent of full-audio scores with no audio input. Among items needing audio, only about 3 to 4 percent need the whole clip; most resolve from fragments. The authors close with guidelines for better evaluation and benchmark design.
arxiv-2604-24701: Bursztein and five colleagues train a single neural network on electromagnetic traces from multiple probe positions to detect side-channel leakage over a larger chip area. Side-channel analysis uses physical measurements during cryptographic operations, and probe placement strongly affects what leaks. Prior work focused on finding hot spots and repositioning. The authors test portability across two independent labs, profiling with one lab's data and attacking the other lab's traces.
arxiv-2604-24801: Carmichael argues that architecture decides whether transformer errors stay visible. Autoregressive transformers make sure errors that confidence monitoring misses. Activation probes catch them only if training leaves a decision signal beyond the output. Adjusting for output confidence removes 60.3 percent of the raw activation-probe signal across 14 models. Most probe signal is just output confidence. Where the signal survives, monitoring succeeds where confidence fails. On downstream QA, a WikiText-trained probe, untuned, catches about one in eight confident errors missed by confidence checks. Its flag rate is 20 percent.
arxiv-2604-24901: Villafaña and nine colleagues ask whether broad-line region profile shape can improve single-epoch black hole mass estimates. The virial coefficient f, meant to capture broad-line region geometry and kinematics, remains a large systematic uncertainty source for active galactic nuclei masses. Updating the sample with ten new sources from CARAMEL dynamical modeling, they again find marginal evidence for that correlation, with slope and scatter consistent with earlier results. If confirmed, line shape could enable empirical f estimates and improve single-epoch masses across cosmic time.
arxiv-2604-25001: Tissot-Daguette and Zhang present cylindrical projections for occupied diffusions. Occupied diffusions give a Markov framework for path-dependent motion. Because that feature is huge, simulation remains intractable. Cylindrical projections mimic the occupation flow with a finite system. The authors prove strong convergence to the first process and derive rates. They test the method with Euler-Maruyama simulations of self-interacting flows and a finance vol model. They also give a weak error study with effects for Monte Carlo methods and derivatives pricing.
arxiv-2604-25101: Shin, Yang and Lee build error estimation for the enriched Galerkin finite element method on linear parabolic equations. The method is known for local conservation and low cost, yet its error analysis for parabolic problems had not been done. With a residual-based approach they prove the estimators reliable and efficient. They then plug the estimators into adaptive mesh refinement, and tests show efficient, dependable error control over time.
arxiv-2604-25201: Bhatt and Kurup present a trust-aware networking framework for secure low-latency failover between communication channels for aerospace and defence. A high-bandwidth primary link, such as satellite or LTE, pairs with a low-power fallback channel, such as radio or mesh, under a zero-trust controller. A real-time intrusion detection system updates node trust scores. When trust or link reliability drops, the controller switches traffic to the secondary channel alone. Simulations show failover under 5 milliseconds with far less packet loss than single-channel or static routing.
arxiv-2604-25501: Acclavio, Straßburger and Zamdzhiev define a notion of proof identity for the logic BV. It is built on atomic flows, viewed as a special form of string diagrams. BV-categories aim to give categorical semantics to BV proofs, but the link between the categories and the logic stayed unclear. No coherence theorem existed, and no settled notion of proof identity existed either. The new identity notion lets the team strengthen the existing notion of BV-category. They then prove the strengthened notion is sound with respect to the logic.
arxiv-2604-25801: Liu proves a surprising reality result for the Jaynes-Cummings memory-kernel generator. The model couples a two-level system to one bosonic mode in cavity quantum electrodynamics. Projecting out the mode leaves a seemingly non-Hermitian generator. Yet its spectrum stays strictly real at every coupling and finite truncation. For a vacuum bath the polynomial factors fully, recovering the dressed-state ladder, lowest mode cut by root two. For thermal states, Cauchy interlacing forces real eigenvalues and a metric proves hidden pseudo-Hermiticity.
arxiv-2604-26101: Gajjala disproves a conjecture about random cycle-factors of directed regular graphs. The conjecture predicted that a disjoint union of complete looped digraphs uniquely maximizes the expected number of cycles. For every degree from three upward, and every multiple of that degree with at least two blocks, the paper constructs a directed regular graph. Its random cycle-factor averages strictly more cycles than the conjectured maximum. The paper also proves the conjectured picture correct in degree two. That gives a sharp split between degree two and all higher degrees.
arxiv-2604-26401: Bullis and six colleagues measured absolute frequencies of two-photon transitions in a cryogenic beam of atomic hydrogen, covering 2S to nS lines with n equal to 8, 9, and 10. Combined with the 1S to 2S frequency, the results yield a root-mean-square proton radius and a Rydberg frequency. Both agree well with the CODATA 2022 recommended values, sharpening a key input to precision atomic physics.
arxiv-2604-26601: Korbel and six colleagues reviewed stochastic thermodynamics, the frame for non-equilibrium processes traced along wavering paths. Work, heat, and entropy production gain meaning per path, not just per ensemble, yielding fluctuation theorems, uncertainty relations, and speed limits tested on many platforms. The review extends the field to memory systems, hidden degrees of freedom, active matter, and optimal-transport geometry. It also surveys large-scale and complex-system challenges plus emerging uses in computing, biology, and social dynamics.
arxiv-2604-26801: Gardiner and five colleagues revisit how low-energy electron neutrinos are absorbed by argon-40, a reaction key to supernova spotting in liquid-argon detectors like DUNE. They refine the MARLEY model, treating unbound nuclear states with a continuum random-phase model that adds forbidden transitions, plus allowed ones from indirect tests. Their cross sections predict a smaller allowed share than before. For a Milky Way burst, MARLEY overstates event yield by about 20 percent, and steeper backward-angle losses make supernova pointing easier than thought.
arxiv-2604-26901: Tringali and Wen study the power semigroup of a numerical semigroup, the family of its non-empty subsets under sumset addition. They show its automorphism group is trivial, meaning the only symmetry is the identity map, and the same holds for the subfamily of subsets containing zero when zero lies in the semigroup. The proofs mix combinatorics and semigroup theory. The result pins down the full symmetry structure of these subset semigroups, leaving no hidden automorphisms.
arxiv-2604-27101: Kundu and Linte propose a two-stage nnUNet tool for left atrial scars in late gadolinium MRI, where scars are rare, the wall thin, and contrast weak. Stage one segments the cavity; stage two derives cavity and wall distance maps, coding voxel place by cavity and wall. This turns intensity-only sorting into anatomy-guided localization, steadying thin-wall learning and blocking invalid predictions. A wall-masked loss with edge supervision restricts learning to the wall, handling imbalance. On LAScarQS 2022 they reach a Dice of 61.1 percent, cutting false positives.
arxiv-2604-27201: Wang and nine colleagues propose Path-Lock Expert, an architecture fix for hybrid-thinking language models with explicit think and no-think modes. Even in no-think mode, current models often leak long self-reflective reasoning, because both modes share the same feed-forward weights. Path-Lock Expert replaces the single MLP in each decoder layer with two locked experts, one per mode, while sharing attention, embeddings, normalization, and the output head. A control-token router picks exactly one expert path for the whole sequence.
arxiv-2604-27301: Guo and three colleagues simulate an isolated elliptical galaxy with both jets and winds. They study churn and star formation cutback in such galaxies. Winds and jets are paired when the infall rate is low, at low infall. Both may matter for active galactic nucleus feedback. Yet prior works typically include only jets with free parameters. Their fluid simulations resolve the Bondi radius for reliable rates. They use parameters from GRMHD simulations. Selectively activating jets and winds reveals their individual and combined effects on churn and central gas entropy.
arxiv-2604-27401: Liu, Li, and Wu introduce perturbation probing, a tool that builds hypotheses about feedforward neurons from two forward passes per prompt, with no backpropagation. Across 13 models, they find opposition circuits, where training suppresses a pretraining tendency, and routing circuits, spread through attention. In safety refusal, about 50 neurons control the refusal template, and removing them flips 80 percent of response formats across 520 prompts with almost no harmful compliance. For language choice, direction injection switches English to Chinese on 99.1 percent of 580 prompts in 3 of 19 models, and fails elsewhere.
arxiv-2604-27801: Blanco-Romero and Almenares Mendoza use majorization to describe the local swap engine behind Gram-Schmidt smoothing in lattice trimming. Each working Lovász swap works like a T-transform, reshaping the log-norm profile, cutting every Schur-convex spread measure. The worst-case GSA shell is the unique lowest-spread profile fitting Lovász gap shape, its slope set by LLL alone. The swap path meets an exact folding rule for variance loss. The viewpoint orders deep-insert rules and suggests Thermal-Adaptive and Geodesic Deep-LLL.
arxiv-2604-27901: Colantoni studies heat flow in a region whose edge reactivity flips as a Markov chain, under a Robin rule. Averaging over heat noise and flips, he frames it with a contraction semigroup on a product space, naming its generator and Feynman-Kac formula. For fixed flip paths, he uses an evolution family and a Feynman-Kac form tied to edge local time of reflected Brownian motion. Fast flips average the system out to a plain Robin problem. The results feed a model of randomly gated cell-membrane receptors.
arxiv-2604-28101: Lima and colleagues map twenty-five years of research on soft skills in agile software teams, analysing nearly a hundred studies from 2000 to 2025. Recurring strengths include communication, adaptability, teamwork and leadership, linked to different agile roles, with Scrum the most adopted approach. Gaps remain, notably few studies on role-specific soft skills, and the findings should help shape curricula, training and workplace practice around human factors.
arxiv-2605-00501:
Yan Lin, Yihong Su, and Yi Yang train financial prediction models on the very score they will be judged by. That score is Rank IC, the rank correlation between a model's predictions and the asset returns that actually follow. Most models instead train on regression losses or generic ranking goals, which can pull against the target metric.

Their method, LambdaRankIC, optimizes Rank IC directly. Ranking is not differentiable, so they derive closed-form expressions for the gradients created by swapping pairs of assets, letting standard gradient training proceed inside the LambdaRank framework. They implement it as a custom objective in a popular boosting library, and prove it optimizes an upper bound on the target. In simulations it recovered true rankings and beat rivals under noisy, heavy-tailed conditions. On real market data it led on Rank IC, stability, monthly return, and Sharpe ratio.
arxiv-2605-01001:
Ludwig Sidenmark and three co-authors present AnimationDiff, a visual tool for comparing generated 3D character animations. New methods now produce many animation variants easily, but choosing the best is hard because of timing misalignment and large amounts of spatial data. Classic creation took major animator effort, and comparing now becomes the bottleneck.

The tool supports side-by-side checks in the intended scene and camera angle. It combines established display methods with easy switching between overlaid and side-by-side views. Filtering handles information overload, and Temporal Lenses display whole animations over time for overview, alignment, and comparison. A user study shows the tool helps with such checks and yields design insights for comparing motion more generally.
arxiv-2605-01301:
Qingzhao Zhang and two co-authors present a stealthy fake-data attack on shared perception for connected and self-driving vehicles. Sharing sensory data improves it, but tampered inputs create security risks. Prior attacks spoof or remove objects, yet how practical they are in dynamic real-world driving was unclear.
