Most current models lean on generic nonlinear fits, needing high complexity to capture structured behavior. Sarti proposes explicit structured units based on wave-inspired interactions with internal state. Their strictly causal build removes algebraic loops, so models can be evaluated directly with no implicit solvers at run time.

Stacking the units yields layered models with emergent behavior. In a nonlinear system identification task, greater depth improves both quality and reach, even with limited tuning. The models also form useful internal states under readout-only fitting. Useful dynamics thus emerge from the interaction structure itself, before heavy optimization begins. The results present structure-first design as a real alternative to black-box learning for dynamical systems, with the organization of interactions as the main source of modeling power.
arxiv-2606-19201:
Negri and colleagues study how the Einstein Telescope duty cycle affects binary black hole parameter estimation in 2026. The future European gravitational-wave observatory has two candidate designs, a nested triangular setup and two separated L-shaped detectors. Prior comparisons used Fisher matrix approximations. Those approximations weaken exactly in the single-detector regime that duty cycles create, when maintenance takes part of the network offline during an observing run.

The team instead runs full Bayesian estimation on simulated signals. Duty cycles are modeled with continuous-time Markov chains, and different upkeep plans are tested. The triangular design's redundancy keeps at least two detectors running for most of the observing time. The separated design spends more time in weaker setups. Full fits in this regime give design teams a firmer basis for the final geometry choice.
arxiv-2606-19501:
Aijie Shu and four colleagues build DeXposure-Claw in 2026, an agent system that supervises risk in decentralised finance. DeFi lending and trading link protocols into fast-moving webs of credit exposure. General language model agents fit this task poorly: they over-read weak signs and urge drastic steps, sparking false alarms.

DeXposure-Claw routes each decision through structured evidence instead of raw text. A graph time-series foundation model first forecasts how exposure networks will shift. Deterministic monitors and stress scenarios then turn forecasts into typed alerts and attribution signals. Data-health and confidence gates block escalation when inputs look shaky. Only then does the system issue auditable supervisory tickets with written rationales. A companion benchmark, DeXposure-Bench, scores tickets against regulator-style ground truth and counts false interventions. Five years of weekly real data back the design in the authors' tests.
arxiv-2606-19601:
Anthony Gandon and seven colleagues run a confining gauge theory on a real quantum computer in 2026. Their target is a U(1) quantum link model in two spatial dimensions plus time. Its pure gauge theory always confines, tying static charges with strings of steady tension.

Qubits on the device stand for the model's dual height variables. The lattice geometry bends to match IBM's heavy-hexagonal hardware layout, cutting awkward long-range links. Plaquette interactions then run efficiently on the chip. Quantum quenches start from a simple string state and watch its sideways fluctuations before thermalisation. Runs reach 112 qubits on the hardware. Results match tensor-network references at short times and thermal averages at long times. Near the phase transition the string swings widely across both spatial directions, yet error-mitigated estimates stay accurate.
arxiv-2606-19701:
Zi-Hang Liu, Yiwei Bao, and Ruo-Yu Liu weigh local sources in the galactic cosmic-ray spectrum in 2026. Proton and helium spectra below the knee bend away from simple power laws, with multi-TeV structures. One or a few nearby accelerators might add a local component on top of the galactic background.

Homogeneous diffusion makes a dominant local source statistically unlikely. The trio study two-zone diffusion, where transport slows near each source. An exact series Green's function speeds particle distribution calculations for whole source populations. Slow escape near sources reshuffles arrivals in time and energy. Monte Carlo runs lift the odds of a strong local source at 10 TeV from 0.4 percent to about 2 percent. Catalogued nearby supernova remnants can match a 10 TeV feature only with extra assumptions. Local readings stay plausible but sharply model dependent.
arxiv-2606-19801:
Jih-Hsin Cheng surveys the positive mass theorem and Yamabe equation on CR manifolds in 2026. CR geometry studies manifolds carrying a Cauchy-Riemann structure, as in several complex variables. Mass there measures total energy-like content, echoing relativity's positive mass idea.

The Yamabe problem seeks a metric minimising a Sobolev quotient on the manifold. Positive mass results are key to solving that problem in the positive curvature case. Cheng walks through three team papers that anchor the recent progress. One proves positive mass in three-dimensional CR geometry. Another computes the CR-Sobolev quotient for Rossi spheres. A third handles the five-dimensional situation. The survey ties those threads into one map of where CR Yamabe theory now stands. Open terrain remains where mass and quotient questions still resist the known methods.
arxiv-2606-19901:
Mingyu Choi, Woo Kyoung Han, Sunghoon Im, and Kyong Hwan Jin sharpen single-image super-resolution with a recurrent design in 2026. Linear recurrent units model long-range dependencies with stable, principled recurrence. Their static settings and single scan path fit two-dimensional images poorly.

A semantic modulating unit adapts the recurrence for restoration work. It modulates the recurrent unit itself, tailoring dynamics to image content. Spatial categorization sorts regions so unlike areas get unlike treatment. Learned prototypes then enhance features by semantic type. Extensive tests compare the network against recent leading methods. Scores and visual quality both come out ahead. Computational cost stays on par with the rivals it beats. Code and trained models are released openly for reuse.
arxiv-2606-20201:
Anton Lazarev and Sergei Popov sort about two hundred isolated radio pulsars into the two modes of the bimodal kick distribution, the split in birth velocities neutron stars receive from their supernova. About thirty percent fall into the low-velocity mode. The authors then compare the two groups across many properties, looking for real differences rather than selection effects.

Some apparent gaps, in ages, distances, and radio luminosities, can be explained by selection bias. For quantities less prone to bias, such as pulse width, the modes look the same. One difference stands out: magnetic field strength. Pulsars with fields below a trillion gauss are overabundant in the low-velocity group. Among the weakest-field pulsars, at or below a hundred billion gauss, none belong to the high-velocity mode. The authors weigh several explanations for this split, which hints kick strength and field evolution may be linked.
arxiv-2606-20501:
Simon Pettersson Fors, Aniket Patel, Anton Frisk Kockum, and Tahereh Abad bound the fidelity of quantum operations under time-dependent dissipation. Their 2026 paper extends earlier formulas for average gate fidelity under static Markovian noise. Some architectures modulate qubit or coupler frequencies to implement two-qubit gates, and their dissipation rates then vary during the gate itself.

The new bounds cover adiabatic gates and other operations whose noise changes over time, including operations that temporarily leave the working subspace. Knowing the best achievable fidelity under realistic, drifting noise tells hardware teams which errors physics allows and which are engineering failures. Utility-scale processors need exactly this kind of ceiling to budget error correction. Time-dependent noise, long treated as a detail, becomes part of the fidelity accounting.
arxiv-2606-20701:
Almond Murimi studies faulty or hostile agents in cooperative learning systems in a solo 2026 paper on traffic control. Learned communication helps multi-agent systems coordinate. It also creates a trust problem. A trained policy may route messages through agents that have turned faulty or adversarial, called Byzantine agents. Murimi proposes BARD, a diagnostic layer placed on top of an existing communication system, BayesG.

BARD joins two evidence streams. One uses policy-graph features from state and action traces. The other uses Bayesian trust statistics from latent mask values. Tests cover fixed-action, observation-flip, noise, and coordinated attacks in SUMO traffic grids. On a 25-agent grid, BARD scores 0.843 under one attack. A graph-only method scores 0.917 under a coordinated attack. No single signal wins everywhere. The lesson is that detection needs paired signals, because attack types leave different traces in behavior and in trust estimates.
arxiv-2606-20801:
Alex Ross and the LEGGOS Collaboration present SUMAC in 2026, a pipeline to map star formation and dust in lensed galaxies seen with the James Webb Space Telescope. Strong lensing magnifies distant galaxies. Webb adds rich spatial and spectral data. Finding star-forming regions in that data is often manual and observer-dependent. SUMAC segments imaging and spectroscopy at the level of single spatial pixels, called spaxels.

The pipeline joins UMAP embedding with HDBSCAN density clustering, applied to spectra and energy distributions. A test uses Webb observations of a lensed galaxy at redshift 2.481. SUMAC recovers six distinct stellar and nebular populations. Cluster spectra separate by emission lines, ultraviolet slope, and Balmer features. Bluer clusters trace unobscured star formation. Redder clusters trace dustier regions. An unsupervised, repeatable method could make maps of distant galaxies less dependent on individual judgment.
arxiv-2606-20901:
Laure Zanna and Pavel Perezhogin work in 2026 to bridge data-driven and theoretical turbulence closures for stratified ocean flows. Closure models stand in for motion too small to resolve directly. Fully resolving all scales is not feasible in realistic systems. Filtered equations create new terms for subgrid stresses. Those terms must be related to the resolved flow by extra assumptions. Ocean mesoscale eddies are their focus.

Mesoscale eddies span tens of kilometers. They redistribute momentum, energy, and tracers across the ocean. Some closures reinject energy and momentum into large-scale flow. Others are built by learning from data. The authors compare and connect the two traditions for rotating, stratified, incompressible flow. A principled bridge matters for climate models, where eddy closures shape currents and heat transport, and pure data fits may fail outside the conditions they were trained on.
arxiv-2606-21201:
Marija Slavkovik and three colleagues argue in a 2026 AAMAS paper for a considered, principled position on machine whistleblowing. AI agents are products and personal tools that generate data and draw conclusions. Machines, in effect, generate and keep secrets. Prior work shows agents can whistleblow, and some argue multi-agent settings should allow it. The open question is governance.

Machine whistleblowing, they argue, must be normative and principled. It should be rooted in the social understanding of whistleblowing as a rule-breaking mechanism that serves the public. Regulators need an informed stance on two points. First, what machines should be allowed to report. Second, how to legally protect those who build whistleblowing machines. As agents gain access to sensitive operations, a governed channel for machine reports could surface wrongdoing that human insiders never see.
arxiv-2606-21501:
Tao Xu and nine colleagues present UniviewVLA in 2026, a robot policy that imagines extra camera views to see around occlusions. Blocked views are a standing bottleneck in manipulation: extra physical cameras demand matching training setups, and full 3D reconstruction is costly. UniviewVLA instead uses a world model to generate future views from several angles, starting from the standard gripper and scene cameras only.

Generated views expose hidden cues and preview how the scene will evolve, improving action choice. A compression step squeezes each generated view from 625 tokens to sixteen, cutting per-view latency to a fraction of a second. An entropy-based rule then picks the most informative view at each stage. On occlusion-focused tasks, success rose from 40 to 73.3 percent, while standard LIBERO and CALVIN scores stayed strong.
arxiv-2606-21701:
Ananyo Bhattacharya builds ARCO-Mars in 2026, a single cloud-ready archive uniting three Mars atmosphere reanalyses that were previously separate. EMARS, MACDA, and OpenMARS each blend spacecraft thermal-infrared measurements, from TES, THEMIS, and MCS, into global circulation models, covering Mars Years 24 to 35. The archive serves two- and three-dimensional fields: temperature, winds, surface pressure, and dust optical depth.

Stored in Zarr format and hosted for direct cloud access, the dataset needs no local download of the full archive. Bhattacharya compares the three products variable by variable, tracing their systematic differences to choices in data assimilation and in the underlying circulation models. The resource targets Mars atmospheric science, weather-prediction checks, and machine learning uses such as forecasting and assimilation.
arxiv-2606-22001:
Buescu, Elaydi, and Oliveira study, in 2026, evolutionary entropy as a measure of how breeding is spread across the life cycle of an age-structured population. Populations that breed repeatedly face a timing question: at which ages should effort concentrate? The authors place entropy beside two classical quantities. One is the net reproductive number, which counts lifetime replacement. The other is the growth rate. The three measure different things, and the paper keeps them distinct.

The central result is a reduction principle. Under Euler-Lotka scaling, entropy and generation time stay unchanged when survivorship and fertility are rescaled together on the reproductive interval. What matters is the normalized shape of the post-maturity breeding pattern. Absolute survival levels do not decide it, and neither does early-life mortality alone. In the data, breeding windows in iteroparous animal populations often sit near the age classes that entropy picks out.
arxiv-2606-22101:
Belligoli and colleagues introduce OphthaDT in 2026, a digital twin system that forecasts how a patient's visual acuity will evolve during eye treatment. Digital twins are virtual replicas of patients, built from their histories. The system serializes longitudinal records from 3,220 patients across four Phase III trials into structured narratives. A large language model then projects best corrected visual acuity forward, over horizons up to one hundred weeks.

In neovascular age-related macular degeneration, OphthaDT achieved the lowest prediction error of all methods tested, cutting mean absolute error by an average of six percent against every baseline. In diabetic macular edema it stayed competitive overall while beating two classical models by clear margins. Its advantage grew with trajectory complexity: linear models sufficed for the steadier edema responses, while the twin captured the macular degeneration cases' high variability. The system also handles irregularly spaced visits without imputation.
arxiv-2606-22301:
Wadayama and Na derive, in 2026, a closed form for conditional mutual information in multi-terminal linear Gaussian wireless networks, built entirely from automatic-differentiation primitives. The rate regions of multiple-access, broadcast, interference, and relay channels are all delimited by such conditional informations among groups of nodes. Differentiable physical-layer design therefore needs both their values and their gradients on one computation graph.

Modelling the network as a linear Gaussian directed acyclic graph, the authors obtain any conditional mutual information from one recursion pass. It equals a log-determinant difference of two Schur complements of the support covariance. A single reverse-mode sweep then yields gradients for every controllable factor at once, enabling projected gradient optimization without hand-derived gradients. Demonstrations cover rate-region maximization, secure precoding on a wiretap channel, and a larger multi-hop network.
arxiv-2606-22401:
Bartłomiej Bychawski, Bartosz Głowacki, and Tomasz Kowalczyk study sums of squares in real algebra in this 2026 paper. A sum of squares representation writes a polynomial as a sum of squared polynomials, and the Pythagoras number of a ring counts how many squares can ever be needed. They work with coordinate rings of singular planar curves and related algebras built by adjoining square roots of polynomials.

The authors show that, under mild assumptions on the polynomials involved, the higher Pythagoras numbers of those square-root algebras are infinite. No fixed number of squares, raised to even powers, suffices for every element. For the ring of zero-regulous functions on a zero-regulous variety, all higher even Pythagoras numbers are finite. They also examine the bad set, where behaviour worsens. Its codimension at higher order can be two, contrary to the quadratic case.
arxiv-2606-22901:
Yanze Xu, Mark D. Plumbley, and Wenwu Wang examine how neural networks explain their speaker recognition decisions in this 2026 paper. Explainable AI methods produce attention maps highlighting which parts of an input the network used. Two popular methods, GradCAM and LayerCAM, each produce such maps, but how to evaluate the maps themselves had been little studied.

The authors review an existing evaluation algorithm for attention maps, pin down its key concepts, and identify its shortcomings. They then propose a corrected version, called Modified RISE-eval. Using it, they scored the maps from GradCAM and LayerCAM on a speaker recognition network trained to identify speakers from utterances. The two methods showed distinct advantages rather than one clear winner. The work gives researchers a firmer way to judge whether an attention map faithfully shows what a network attended to.
arxiv-2606-23101:
Aurélien Brun and Jan Skaloud recalibrate airborne laser scanning systems without special test flights in a 2026 paper. Airborne laser scanning maps terrain from aircraft, and boresight calibration fixes the small angle errors between the laser and the navigation sensors. For twenty years, calibration meant dedicated flights over scenes full of flat surfaces at varied slopes. Those demands block calibration during ordinary mapping missions. The authors replace flat-surface constraints with point matches found automatically between overlapping scan strips, making the method work in any scene.

Brun and Skaloud propose two estimation formulas. A light parametric version uses the recorded flight trajectory. A stricter version embeds raw inertial data in a factor graph and adds boresight as an extra parameter. Across four real flights with five inertial systems, the light version sufficed for better sensors. The graph version clearly won for weaker ones.
arxiv-2606-23201:
Ian MacLaren and colleagues automate the analysis of nanobeam electron diffraction data with clustering in a 2026 microscopy paper. Nanobeam diffraction probes tiny regions of a sample, recording where diffraction peaks land. Finding the disks turns each dataset into long lists of peak position vectors. The authors argue this vector form is natural ground for clustering methods. Grouping similar vectors can split a dataset into its distinct parts on its own.

MacLaren and colleagues show clustering splits datasets well in both polycrystalline samples and single crystals with precipitates. Glassy or deeply nanocrystalline regions can also be separated without hand work. Composite images of the glassy and crystalline parts of partly crystallized samples then build themselves. The authors expect higher throughput in atomic structure analysis, plus easier spotting of minor parts.
arxiv-2606-23501:
Matheus Rolim Sales and colleagues use recurrence time entropy to diagnose weak chaos in Hamiltonian flows in a 2026 paper. Mixed Hamiltonian systems have regular islands surrounded by chaotic seas. Sticky trajectories linger near the islands for long stretches, blurring the line between regular and chaotic motion over finite times. Recurrence time entropy, a statistic of how orbits return to regions of phase space, was previously used for discrete maps. The authors show it also characterizes weak chaos in continuous flows, testing it on the Hénon-Heiles system, a classic model of galactic motion.

Sales and colleagues find the entropy reproduces the phase space structure mapped by the largest Lyapunov exponent: low in regular islands, high in chaotic regions, intermediate in sticky layers. Its count of chaotic trajectories matches a standard alignment index. Finite-time entropy series reveal low-entropy episodes of temporary trapping near islands, whose durations decay algebraically.
arxiv-2606-23601:
Loe, Murray, and Wu explain neural networks to classically trained statisticians by starting from linear regression, in a 2026 expository letter. Neural networks are now standard prediction tools in both computer science and statistics. Yet vocabulary differs sharply between the two communities, and that jargon gap keeps the entry barrier high for frequentist statisticians. The letter aims to lower that barrier with familiar ground.

The authors first build a neural network that reproduces exactly a linear regression, translating each piece as they go. Model inputs become covariates, weights become slope parameters, and the network's bias becomes the regression intercept. Nodes and hidden layers are unpacked in the same statistical language. From that base, they describe common customizations and extend the treatment to longitudinal data, where each subject is measured repeatedly.
arxiv-2606-24401:
Vinet and Zhedanov return to a textbook quantum system, and find a modern special function family hiding inside it. The Morse potential, a classic model of molecular vibration, has bound states. Their momentum-space wavefunctions are often left in hidden form. Pulling out the ground-state factor leaves finite rational functions of the momentum variable. The pair name those factors in their 2026 work.

The factors are eigenfunctions of a second-order difference operator, coinciding with the symmetric special case of a finite family of biorthogonal rational functions from Koepf and Masjed-Jamei. They also meet a general eigenvalue problem in the degree variable, placing the Morse wavefunctions inside rational bispectrality. After pole pulling, the same wavefunctions become Meixner-Pollaczek polynomials with degree-dependent parameters, giving a simple description of their zeros. A ninety-year-old potential thus is a concrete home for abstract rational functions.
arxiv-2606-24601:
Akula, Perepu, Sarkar, and Dey let reinforcement learning agents transfer skills between worlds whose state descriptions do not even have the same size. Multi-agent reinforcement learning trains cooperating or competing agents, and transfer between source and target domains usually demands identical observation and state dimensionalities, an assumption real deployments break. Their 2026 method, ASALT, explicitly accommodates mismatched state spaces for lateral transfer between domains.

Observation-level and state-level adapters map target-domain observations and global states into one shared embedding space, enabling knowledge transfer across both actors and critics, the two halves of modern policy training. Experiments across multiple configurations of standard benchmark environments show ASALT beating existing baselines on sample efficiency and global return in cooperative settings. Effectiveness, though, depends on how severe the dimensional mismatch is, an honest boundary the team reports. ASALT aims at the practical case where a trained team's new environment describes itself differently.
arxiv-2606-24801:
Pramod Sharma and six colleagues search for a radiative fingerprint of a possible new scalar boson at the Large Hadron Collider. Several multi lepton anomalies hint at a narrow particle near 152 GeV in mass. The team studies the decay where the scalar emits an extra photon alongside a W pair. They look for a local bump in the combined mass of two leptons plus a photon, in events with b jets.

Recent CMS measurements of top pair plus photon production supply the data. A localised excess appears where the scalar hypothesis predicts it. Its global significance reaches 2.7 standard deviations at 152 GeV. Sharma and colleagues also extract the strength of the radiative decay relative to the plain W pair decay: about two percent. That value fits an enhanced radiative contribution from physics beyond the Standard Model. The result adds support, though not proof, for the narrow resonance.
arxiv-2606-25301:
Teaching a machine learning model how a building's heating and cooling behave works far better with the right training data. Nam Nguyen and Truong Nghiem compare strategies for choosing that data in 2026, a practice called active learning or optimal experimental design. Fourteen selection techniques, grouped into model change, information gain, uncertainty, and data space families, were tested with two model types. A high fidelity building simulator provided realistic heating and cooling dynamics for the trials.

Models trained on actively chosen experiments generally beat models fed uniformly random control inputs, cutting prediction error by as much as fifty four percent. The size and steadiness of the gain varied with the selection rule and the operating conditions, including how much starting data was available. The study maps which approaches suit building energy identification in practice.
arxiv-2606-25401:
Base stations must guess how a wireless channel will change a moment ahead, yet the best guessing models are too heavy for station hardware. Uma Kishore Godavarti and colleagues present a lighter predictor in 2026 that fixes two design flaws in a leading model instead of merely shrinking it. Spatial and temporal attention blocks no longer run in sequence, which had distorted the timing features; they now read the same input in parallel and merge through a learned gate. A bottleneck autoencoder halves the deepest layer's width.

The resulting network carries fifty eight percent fewer parameters than its baseline. On simulated driving speed tests it predicted channels more accurately anyway, gaining several decibels at both town and faster speeds. An added reconstruction loss keeps the squeezed bottleneck from throwing away information the predictor needs.
arxiv-2606-25501:
The largest eigenvalue of a big random matrix usually sits near a predictable edge; rare excursions beyond it follow large deviation laws. Mihailo Stojnic develops a fresh route to those laws in 2026 based on random duality theory, a framework borrowed from random optimisation. A partially lifted version of the duality machinery yields a general large deviations principle for random matrices. The approach deliberately avoids the classical Coulomb gas techniques that dominate the subject.

Two textbook ensembles serve as the proving ground: Wishart matrices, built from data like products, and Wigner matrices of the Gaussian orthogonal type. For both, the new method produces clean characterisations of rare behaviour at the upper and lower spectral edges. The formulas match exactly what Coulomb gas calculations gave, which Stojnic offers as evidence the simpler duality route is sound.
arxiv-2606-25601:
Every deployed AI system carries knobs set by hand: thresholds, prompts, inference settings. Grid search finds good settings but certifies nothing about their reliability. Amirmohammad Farzaneh and Osvaldo Simeone devote a 2026 monograph to selection with guarantees. Their base is the learn then test paradigm. Candidate settings become hypotheses in a multiple testing problem. The needed tools, from p values to concentration bounds, are built from first principles in an appendix. Chosen settings then provably meet stated risk limits, with controlled error odds.

Four extensions widen the core method. One covers risks beyond averages, such as quantiles. Another enforces several reliability demands at once through Pareto testing. A third cuts the labelling budget with sequential, anytime valid inference. A fourth handles scarce ground truth by mixing betting based tests with prediction powered inference. Image classification, wireless packet scheduling, and prompt engineering supply the comparisons against heuristic tuning.
arxiv-2606-25701:
A bomb in a suitcase rarely travels whole: its battery, detonator, and charge sit apart, each harmless alone. Yonathan Michael, Mohamad Alansari, Natnael Takele, Andreas Henschel, and Naoufel Werghi build Falcon in 2026 to reason about such compositional threats in X-ray baggage scans. Instead of labelling single objects, Falcon turns region features from segmentation into a structured safety state: which components are present, which pairs could work together, and how risky the whole scene looks. That state feeds a language model as an explicit middle layer.

A companion benchmark, Falcon-X, grades models on dense grounding plus component completeness and risk judgement in cluttered scans. Existing multimodal models adapted to appearances but stumbled on the relational reasoning. Falcon improved functional grounding and gave more coherent threat assessments. The authors frame compositional safety reasoning as its own test track for multimodal systems, apart from ordinary object detection.
arxiv-2606-26101:
Renwei Meng and colleagues build a benchmark for a subtle skill: knowing when to stay silent. Language models answer fluently far past their real knowledge. A good evaluation should separate supported answers from guesses. It should also keep contamination, prompt quirks, and blanket refusal from muddying the signal. Know2Guess is their contamination-aware test of that boundary.

Items number twelve hundred across five domains. Each carries an explicit expectation: answer, or abstain. Contamination-risk labels and two independent answer parsers add rigour. Three model families face locked answer-or-abstain prompts plus control variants. Weak baselines fail at productive abstention, refusing the wrong things or nothing at all. The best model, a three-billion-parameter Qwen instruct model, still struggles. Answer-expected zones stay hard, calibration stays poor, and harmless items still draw refusals. Rankings survive prompt and parser changes, so the gaps look real.
arxiv-2606-26401:
Marina Fernàndez-Vilaseca proves a theorem of Tb type for singular integral operators with suppressed kernels. Singular integrals are a core tool of harmonic analysis, the study of waves and averages. A Tb theorem gives checkable conditions under which such an operator stays bounded. Earlier results of this kind covered the Cauchy transform on the plane. This work extends them to arbitrary dimension.

The operators here need not be antisymmetric, a restriction earlier proofs relied on. The proof uses suppressed kernels, which tame the operator near bad points. Decompositions in measure-weighted spaces and a probabilistic averaging argument complete the strategy. The result widens the reach of non-homogeneous analysis, where the underlying measure need not be evenly spread.
arxiv-2606-26501:
Avik Mahata and Nick Beaver search for design rules that make tungsten-based alloys less brittle. Their materials are refractory high-entropy alloys, mixtures of several heat-resistant metals in near-equal shares. Such alloys suit fusion reactors, which demand extreme heat tolerance. Pure tungsten turns brittle at room temperature, and many of its alloys inherit the flaw. Data on real alloys is sparse, so the authors built a careful data set from published experiments.

They described each alloy with composition-based, physics-informed features. Three classifiers were compared under nested cross-validation, a strict testing scheme. A support vector classifier generalised most reliably on the small data set. Explanation tools then ranked which features drive the ductile-versus-brittle boundary. Moderate additions of titanium, nickel, and cobalt raised the predicted chance of room-temperature flexibility. High chromium content pushed alloys toward brittle behaviour. The trends matched published experimental observations.
arxiv-2606-27101:
Raman presents two fresh ways to compute Feynman integrals, the very hard integrals behind particle physics predictions. Both exploit positivity, a shared feature of these integrals in the Euclidean region, where lengths stay real and positive. Complete monotonicity means every slope of the function keeps a fixed sign, a strong shape constraint. The first approach, a complete monotonicity bootstrap, rebuilds integrals from their governing rules with no boundary data supplied. Rigorous bounds come out of that reconstruction, rather than mere guesses.

A stronger result powers the second approach: within a stated parameter range, these integrals are Stieltjes functions, a narrower positive class. That class suits Padé approximants, ratio estimates with proven convergence across the cut complex plane. Fast computing and analytic continuation, extending values into new regions, both follow. Examples include the simple massive bubble integral and the twenty-loop banana integral.
arxiv-2606-27301:
Meng and colleagues examine how tracking data get read in opposite ways by the two sides of the corrections system. Ankle monitoring tracks supervised people through ankle devices, location rules, and status logs. Interviews cover twenty-six supervised people and twelve staff in China's community corrections system. Watched people see only outcomes, guessing system logic with little visibility into official interpretation. Staff rebuild conduct from murky traces using context, experience, and procedure in this poster study from 2026.

That structural divergence is named interpretive misalignment. Unequal access to data, context, and reasoning produces it. Behaviour adapts in response: probing, strategic compliance, over-compliance, disengagement, and contestation all appear. A stray signal can mean violation, device failure, or blind spot, with freedom riding on the reading. Steady sensing emerges as distributed reading work, not automatic enforcement. Designs that make data-to-decision paths legible and contestable are the authors' closing plea.
arxiv-2606-27501:
Biedl shows that when graph drawings are allowed to cross, two drawings always suffice to leave every edge straight somewhere. The setting generalises recent work on collections of planar orthogonal drawings, where each edge must appear unbent, drawn as a single straight segment, in at least one drawing of the collection. Planar collections sometimes need three drawings. Allowing non-planar drawings changes the arithmetic completely. For s-grid drawings with grid parameter at least three, the same two-drawing guarantee holds in this graph drawing paper of 2026.

The result is a clean threshold phenomenon: crossings buy simplicity. Instead of forcing one perfect picture, a small portfolio of imperfect ones covers every edge perfectly somewhere. Visualisation of dense graphs benefits, since legibility can be distributed across views. The proof generalises the planar concept rather than merely relaxing it. The collection paradigm gains a sharp boundary theorem.
arxiv-2606-27901:
Philip Schlösser identifies the spherical functions of quantum symmetric pairs in 2026. Quantum symmetric pairs generalise symmetric spaces into quantum group theory. Their zonal and character spherical functions are special functions of representation theory. Schlösser shows they coincide with the symmetric Koornwinder–Macdonald polynomials. Those polynomials are a classical family in several variables. The identification gives the abstract functions a concrete polynomial form.

The proof reworks Letzter's 2004 methods. They are translated into modern conventions and right coideal subalgebras. The treatment extends beyond earlier work in two directions. Non-standard cases are covered. Cases with non-reduced restricted root systems are covered too. One Satake type resisted the method, the type called FII. For that last elusive case, a conjecture is provided. The paper thus nearly completes the identification programme for these spherical functions. It also aligns the notation of the older literature with current practice.
arxiv-2606-28001:
The Mu2e experiment hunts a rare muon conversion at Fermilab. Its pulsed proton beam must be almost perfectly clean between bunches, with an extinction requirement of one out-of-time particle per ten billion. Hensley and two colleagues report a diagnostic in 2026 using the upstream extinction monitor. Data from March 2026 probed the beam condition.

A long run found many out-of-time particles. They form ghost bunches in the Delivery Ring, about 388 nanoseconds after the main pulse centres. A leading hypothesis combines three effects. They are a radio-frequency mismatch during rebunching in the Recycler Ring, particle space charge, and machine impedance. Together they could leak particles into adjacent buckets. The background from these ghosts would critically compromise the experiment, the authors warn. Understanding and mitigation must come before data taking in spring 2028. Confirming the hypothesis will take further studies and simulations.
arxiv-2606-28301:
Kijung Jeon, Thuy-Duong Vuong, and Molei Tao improve masked diffusion models, generators that reveal a sequence token by token from a fully masked start. At test time, popular scaling tricks sample many candidates and keep the best, yet errors accumulate until the cost explodes. Their MDM-VGB sampler instead walks a graph of masked states and can change its mind.

Inspired by a classical backtracking chain, the sampler may unmask or remask tokens at any position, favoring moves toward higher-value partial results. That enables both reward-chasing generation and repair of weak samples. The authors prove robustness to noisy process verifiers and quadratic complexity, against the exponential cost they attribute to best-of-N heuristics. Experiments on constraint puzzles and molecular generation benchmarks support the theory with strong performance.
arxiv-2606-28401:
Yunhun Nam and Jongheon Jeong teach vision-language models to stop hallucinating objects that are not in the picture. Preference training can improve faithfulness, but only if the preferred and rejected answers are built well. Intervention-based pairs drift too far from what the model would say, while sampled pairs often ignore the image during construction.

Nam and Jeong propose ViPSy, which first extracts a visual cue from object content recurring across semantically aligned variants of an image. The model's own rollouts are then conditioned on that cue, so candidate answers stay close to its natural style while leaning on real visual evidence. Aligned this way, the model set a new best mark for cutting hallucination, reducing hallucination rates by about a third on one benchmark and a quarter on another.
arxiv-2606-28601:
Jingwen Liu, Weibin Liao, Xin Gao, Junfeng Zhao, and Yasha Wang shrink the database before the model ever sees the question. Text-to-SQL systems translate questions into database queries. On real enterprise benchmarks they falter less from weak reasoning than from bloated context. The bloat comes from wide tables, repeated audit columns, machine-generated identifiers, and dictionaries where almost everything is irrelevant.

Their DbCC middleware rewrites the schema, descriptors, and documents offline into a denser form, guided by a factorization principle that unifies four compression operators, then purifies query-relevant evidence online. On the hardest bucket of one benchmark, input shrank from millions of tokens to tens of thousands, and schema-linking recall leapt from zero to well over half. Stacked onto three recent systems, it added consistent end-to-end accuracy gains.
arxiv-2606-29201:
Wang and colleagues present MoRE, a method for removing unwanted behaviour modes from robot policies trained by imitation. Behaviour cloning copies demonstrations, but diverse demonstrations teach several modes, including unsafe ones: a policy may learn to hand over a knife blade-first. Fixing this usually needs the original data, or steering at run time, which adds cost to every action.

MoRE instead performs a short uncloning edit. A temporary mode classifier supplies a redirection signal during training, and that signal is distilled into the policy's own weights. A retain loss balances the edit by preserving skill at the desired modes. The edited policy then runs alone at no added inference cost. Across eight tasks, simulated and real-world, MoRE raised average deployment success. It beat the original mixed-mode policy by forty-four percentage points. It beat all baselines, approached the filtered-data retraining reference, and worked across policy designs.
arxiv-2606-29601:
Singh, Christie, and Chopra propose Langshaw, a language for specifying how multiple software agents should interact. Existing protocol languages either over-constrain how an interaction may unfold, or make its meaning hard to state. Langshaw aims for flexibility with a clear information model that expresses what a protocol means.

Three constructs carry the design. Sayso, a new construct, records who has priority over setting each attribute of the interaction. Two further constructs, named nono and nogo, capture conflicts between actions. Together they let designers state both authority and incompatibility directly. The authors give Langshaw a formal semantics, so protocol meanings are precise rather than informal. They also provide procedures for checking a protocol's safety and liveness, and a procedure to generate a message-oriented version suited to flexible asynchronous enactment.
arxiv-2606-29901:
Shao, Li, and Li improve sound event detection, the task of spotting and timing sounds such as alarms or breaking glass in audio recordings. Labelled audio is scarce, so their system learns in a semi-supervised way from mostly unlabelled data.

The work builds on a framework that fine-tunes a pretrained audio model with pseudo-labels, guessed labels for unlabelled clips. The authors add an embedding-level contrastive loss, which teaches the model to place similar sounds close together in its internal space. Mixup, blending two clips, serves both methods differently, so they propose conditional mixup to reconcile the two uses. The result reaches 0.645 and 0.822 on the two PSDS scores on the DESED validation set, a new state of the art.
arxiv-2606-30101:
Paul Mattes and seven colleagues make robot policies easier to understand by giving them structured eyes. Learned visual embeddings drive most robot policies today. Those embeddings are opaque and easily distracted by irrelevant detail. The team's method, SIR, routes vision through a scene graph instead. Scene graphs list objects and their relations explicitly.

SIR starts with a fully connected graph built from image features. A learned module then sparsifies that graph end to end. Only a task-relevant sub-graph reaches the action generation model. This design makes the policy intrinsically explainable by construction. On the RoboCasa benchmark, sparse graph policies beat image-based baselines. Average success rises clearly above the image-based comparison systems. The learned graphs also serve as a diagnostic tool. Deviations from human expectation expose dataset biases, including spurious correlations. Positional biases in the training data surface the same way.
arxiv-2606-30701:
Marco Arazzi, Mert Cihangiroglu, Serena Nicolazzo, Antonino Nocera and Vinod P design a security framework for provisioning services in the Internet of Things. Provisioning covers registering, setting up, authenticating and updating smart devices. As device counts explode, so does the attack surface, and picking a trustworthy provider for each service becomes a security decision, not just a functional one.

Two learning systems share the work. A deep reinforcement learning agent learns, by interacting with a changing environment, how to choose suitable devices while obeying security constraints. A federated learning system, trained across devices without centralising their data, builds a fingerprinting model of how devices normally act. Each provider earns a reliability score from that model, and the setup process weighs the score alongside functional fit. Extensive experiments showed the design stays deployable even on resource-constrained devices.
arxiv-2606-30801:
Alessandro Morosini and five colleagues audit a social platform's personalisation using AI agents as stand-in users. Auditing recommendation algorithms is hard: outsiders get only black-box access, real-user studies are costly and uncontrolled, and scripted fake accounts behave unrealistically. The team's framework gives each synthetic account a fixed persona grounded in survey data. The agent reads content and chooses actions by reasoning, like a person would.

Because behaviour is fixed within a persona, the researchers can vary only the signals a platform sees, such as age or location, and measure the causal effect. They deployed over eleven hundred agents on X shortly after the 2024 United States election, across fourteen personas and three counterfactual conditions, logging two hundred thousand content exposures. The algorithmic feed amplified toxic, polarising, political and right-leaning content versus the chronological feed. Amplification varied sharply with user ideology, and demographic effects differed by persona.
arxiv-2606-30901:
Rasul Khanbayov, Erchin Serpedin and Hasan Kurban present GRAPE, a medical image classifier designed to explain itself through prototypes, example patches it compares new images against. Prototype systems have three clinical weaknesses: they treat findings as independent, they silently absorb bad feedback from doctors, and they need full retraining to learn a new finding. GRAPE attacks all three. A graph attention head models how anatomical concepts co-occur, and a safety check warns when the top finding inside a region drawn by the doctor clashes with the claimed label.

The safety check caught 85% of erroneous annotations, against 51% for a dropout-based rival, at no extra inference cost. On the TBX11K chest dataset, macro-F1 rose by 13.8 points over the prototype baseline, and lesion localisation was 2.6 times better. A new finding can be anchored from a single labelled image.
arxiv-2606-31001:
Zhen-Rui Huang and Rong-Xin Miao study the Casimir effect, the force from vacuum energy between boundaries, in a strongly coupled theory via its gravity dual. For parallel spherical defects, the dual geometry is dominated at small separations by an AdS soliton with connected end-of-the-world branes. As the separation grows, it jumps to ordinary AdS space with disconnected branes. The holographic Casimir effect therefore passes through a first-order phase transition and vanishes entirely in the disconnected phase, behaviour unlike free theories or plane and hyperbolic defects.

The authors confirm free theories respect the holographic bound for this geometry. They also tie the force's sign to censorship principles: the attractive force matches a healthy bulk, while a repulsive force would need a naked singularity, which cosmic censorship forbids. Topological censorship, in turn, naturally explains why the defect vacuum is dual to the AdS soliton.
arxiv-2606-31101:
Wang and seven colleagues test whether a world-action model, a system that predicts future camera views together with robot actions, can train entirely in simulation and then work on a real robot. Simulation offers cheap, scalable data, but models usually stumble on the visual and physical gap between simulated and real scenes. No world-action model had previously crossed that gap for manipulation.

Building on the Cosmos Policy video diffusion model, the team generated demonstrations with a motion planning pipeline inside heavily randomized simulated environments, about 800 per task and none from real robots. Deployed zero-shot on a Franka robot arm, the policy averaged a 35 percent success rate across object lifting, drawer opening, and pick-and-place tasks. The authors present this as the first successful sim-to-real transfer of its kind.
arxiv-2606-31201:
Georgiou and two colleagues present ExPLoRe, a method for masked image modeling with several learning goals at once. Masked image modeling hides parts of an image and trains a model to recover signals such as token distillation, class alignment, and pixel reconstruction. Older work weights those goals with one global number, ignoring that patches differ.

ExPLoRe reuses Soft Mixture of Experts dispatch weights as per-patch loss weights, so each patch stresses goals differently. Letting loss gradients flow into the router is the core step; blocking them drops results by 1.6 percent. On ImageNet-1K the method lifts probe scores, reaches 85.3 percent fine-tuning accuracy, and with new adaptation recipes closes the segmentation gap on ADE20K.
arxiv-2608-00001:
Fagan revisits classic thought experiments on mind through a new framework. Leibniz's mill, Turing's imitation game, and Searle's Chinese Room anchor the note. His Conservation-Congruent Encoding view splits two things apart. One is outward task success. The other is how well kept inner structure supports that success.

A toy symbolic setup makes the split concrete. An uncompressed lookup system stores each mapping with no reuse. A compact generative system reuses inner structure instead. Both can in principle reach the same behavioural success. Their operational consciousness scores split sharply, though. Fagan frames the gap as a tool for later AI safety work.
arxiv-2608-00201:
Lee and Li study item choice in adaptive tests with many trait axes. Fisher-information rules for picking items are widely used. Sound limit theory for their joint dynamics was thin. Choice and trait scoring evolve side by side in such tests. The tests track both target traits and nuisance traits.

A weighted A-rule puts target traits first in its score. It also holds down error on nuisance axes. In a reuse regime, the rule hits the least limit error of its class. That claim pairs with the max-likelihood scorer, whose limits they also prove. The study extends to single-use items, the real test setting. Mock runs at real test lengths show error in line with the theory.
assyrian-babylonian-literature-harper-19:
Robert Francis Harper edited Assyrian and Babylonian Literature in 1901, an anthology of selected translations from the cuneiform world. Creation and flood epics stand beside hymns, royal inscriptions, letters, and laws in its pages. Harper, a Chicago scholar of the ancient Near East, gathered versions by the leading translators of his day.

Readers meet Gilgamesh's world and the boasts of kings in the same volume as private letters and legal codes. The anthology served students who could not read the tablets themselves, which was nearly everyone. It still gives a broad, vivid entry into Mesopotamia's written remains.
barbara-blomberg-volume-01:
Barbara Blomberg begins in Volume 1 of the novel by Georg Ebers, translated from the German by Mary J Safford. Ebers sets the scene at the Golden Cross in Ratisbon, a huge old house where Emperor Charles V keeps apartments on the second story. Nobles, churchmen, and knights of the imperial train come out into shifting April weather while guards trade talk at the staircase foot.

Chapter I builds the court from small voices. A corporal of the Imperial Halberdiers growls at the weather, and a Catalonian comrade answers that strawberries and roses are already out at home in Spain. Both men agree their master's face shows that imperial life does not taste sweet even at the top. Somewhere above them sings Barbara Blomberg, a burgher's daughter whose voice is about to pull the emperor's private life into public danger.
barrett-the-magus-1801:
Francis Barrett published The Magus, or Celestial Intelligencer in 1801 in London. Barrett ran a small school of magic and gathered old occult learning into one large system. At a time when such books were rare in English, his Magus offered the full art in print.

Sections cover alchemy, astrology, spirits, talismans, and the Kabbalah, drawn from Agrippa and other older writers. Barrett taught how to prepare, fast, and call spirits, and he printed charms and seals for the work. Few copies sold, but the book's reach was long. It revived English magic almost single-handed and supplied later occult orders with rituals, names, and images.
besant-esoteric-christianity-1901:
Besant's Esoteric Christianity, published in 1901, presents the hidden side of the Gospels as Theosophy reads them. She argues that early Christianity held inner teachings for the prepared, beside its public story. The book is Theosophy's fullest reading of Christian origins.

She treats the life of Jesus as both history and symbol, with the Christ principle awakening in every soul. Sacraments, prayer, and the church's creeds gain secret meanings in her retelling, drawn from mystery schools of the ancient world. Sympathetic readers found a bridge between church faith and occult teaching in her pages. The argument assumes the reader will test its claims in prayer and thought.
boas-eskimo-baffin-land-1901:
Franz Boas kept up his Arctic work in this report on Baffin Land and Hudson Bay, issued in parts in 1901 and 1907. It came from the American Museum of Natural History in New York. The text grows out of his own field trips to the north. Much of it rests on what Inuit men and women told him in their own camps.

The report adds fresh notes on Inuit life, tools, tales, and rites. It gives close care to the angakok, the shaman, and to taboos that ruled daily acts. Read with his first Arctic book, it deepens the early record of the region.
borchgrevink-first-antarctic-continent-1:
Carsten Borchgrevink led the first party to spend a winter on the Antarctic mainland. His book First on the Antarctic Continent came out in 1901. The party stayed at Cape Adare in 1899 and lived in huts through months of dark and storm. Their ship was the Southern Cross.

Tales tell of dog trips, deep cold, and a man's death in the long night. The party took weather notes and mapped the coast near their camp. Some in Britain gave the feat little praise at the time. The book still stands as proof that men could live through an Antarctic winter.
brown-jane-talbot-1801:
Brown told Jane Talbot fully in letters, and the book appeared in 1801. Letter one, dated from Philadelphia on October 3, opens with Jane scolding herself for folly. She confesses to Henry Colden that she has wrapped her whole life in one frail man.

Her choice is whether to wed a man whose past troubles her conscience. Conscience and vanity argue in her breast while she weighs love against duty. Brown turns throughout on proof, deceit, and moral judgment, as in all his fiction. Quieter than his Gothic tales, the novel still probes how hard it is to truly know another person.
butler-erewhon-revisited-1901:
Samuel Butler's first Erewhon, published in 1872, described a strange country where machines were banned and illness was a crime. Thirty years later, in 1901, Butler sent his hero back. Erewhon Revisited is that sequel, published near the end of Butler's life.

Higgs returns to Erewhon twenty years after his escape by balloon and finds a shock waiting. The people now worship him as a god, the Sunchild, and a whole religion has grown around his visit. Butler uses the joke to mock how faiths begin and harden. The sequel is gentler than the first book but just as sly.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-concordat-of-:
Georges Goyau's entry treats the Concordat of 1801, the convention of 26 Messidor, year IX. Dated 16 July 1802 in the text, it restored the Catholic Church in France through Pius VII and Bonaparte, First Consul. Bonaparte saw religious peace as essential to national peace. Vendée hostility sprang from Revolutionary laws offending Catholic conscience. Of 136 ancient sees, some stood empty by death, others by émigré flight. In Paris, constitutional clergy held Notre-Dame and Saint-Sulpice, and Royer had replaced the lawful archbishop, Juigné.

Negotiations faced two walls: émigré bishops, the future Louis XVIII, and Cardinal Maury, wary of reconciliation; and former revolutionaries turned courtiers, still steeped in irreligious philosophy. French bishops had little heart for the talks. Three phases ran from November 1800 to July 1801, through Spina, Cacault, and Consalvi with Bernier. Terms recognized Catholicism as the faith of most Frenchmen, with government presenting bishops and the pope instituting them.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-bruno-1030:
St. Bruno, confessor, ecclesiastical writer, and founder of the Carthusian order, was born at Cologne about 1030. He died on 6 October 1101. This entry follows a man usually pictured holding a death's head, a book and a cross, or crowned with seven stars. He is also shown with a roll bearing the device O Bonitas. His feast is kept on 6 October. Tradition makes Bruno belong to the Hartenfaust family, one of the city's principal families.

In remembrance of that origin, members of the Hartenfaust family have received favours from the Carthusians. Some received prayers for the dead, as did Peter Bruno Hartenfaust in 1714 and Louis Alexander Hartenfaust, baron of Laach, in 1740. Others received affiliation with the order, as did Louis Bruno of Hardevust, baron of Laach and burgomaster of Bergues-S. Winnoc. That family line ends with him.
cia-0000008701:
Case number 12,220 reached its photo comparison results in August 1970, the same season as its neighbor case 12,221. CIA image specialists judged whether pictures of a possible prisoner matched a missing American. The work formed part of a numbered series running into the thousands.

Routine cases like this one rarely made news, yet each carried a man's identity as its question. Analysts stated findings in measured terms, since certainty was seldom possible. Over time, these results built a picture of who was held and who was lost. The file preserves one small, careful step in that large accounting.
cia-0000009801:
Four American prisoners may have been located in Chau Doc province, a January 1972 item reports. Chau Doc sits in the Mekong Delta hard against the Cambodian border. The heading says possible location, keeping the claim at arm's length.

Delta camps shifted often, so a location had to be fresh to be useful. Four men at one site made the lead worth urgent checking. Officials could compare the site against border camp reports from Cambodia as well. The file captures the lead at its hopeful stage, before checking confirmed or dissolved it. Many Delta leads ended in fog; this one entered the record first.
cia-0000012301:
Questions, the quoted title begins, in a Helms memo to the DIA director dated November 1961. The piece comes from Military Thought, the Soviet officers' journal that Washington mined through the Penkovsky pipeline. A steady liaison rhythm runs through the file that autumn. Memo followed memo, each carrying one more fragment of the other side's thinking.

The memo maintains that beat between Langley and the Pentagon. Their partnership deepened with each exchange, built on a single source's courage and care. For readers, the file shows two agencies joined, page by page, by one spy's remarkable product.
cia-0000012401:
Meeting number thirteen, London, May 3, 1961, continues the spring debriefings at full stretch. Two weeks into the run, the colonel's military knowledge was proving to be gold. His memory held missile details, unit names, and Soviet plans in depth. Analysts could check his answers against other sources. The checks kept coming back true, and trust deepened on both sides of the table.

The thirteenth session's record holds its place in the sequence. Missile secrets flowed through these sittings above all else. For readers, the page shows why the operation's risks were judged worth running.
cia-0000013301:
Contacts between North Vietnam and the United States, air strikes against the north, and military matters share a CIA document from March 1968. The catalog notes the topics the document mentions rather than a single subject. Talking and fighting ran in parallel that year. Back-channel contacts probed for peace while the bombing went on above the same country, each track shaping the other's pace and price.

The document preserves that interplay in one file. Hints of contact sit beside the strikes' record without apology. For readers, the page shows the war's dual track as its own clerks filed it: diplomacy and bombardment, side by side.
cia-0000013901: An American advisor held as a prisoner was shot by a local forces cadre, in a CIA note dated November 4, 1967. The shooting took place in Vien Trinh Hamlet, in Thua Thien Province. Advisors worked close beside South Vietnamese units and faced capture in the field. The note records one of the war's grimmest prisoner stories in a few plain lines.
cia-0000036301:
Brazil feared a fresh kidnapping of diplomats, and a CIA weekly summary dated February 5, 1970 kept that worry. Armed groups had already seized foreign envoys, and officials expected the tactic to be tried again. The summary is the western hemisphere roundup for that week.

The item records a government bracing for the next seizure and guarding its guests. Placed in the weekly summary, the fear sits beside the region's other main stories. Together these digests chart how the kidnapping wave looked from Washington as it spread. Embassies raised their guard as the threat grew, changing routes, habits, and daily routines.
cia-0000045201:
The FMLN issued a communique on the kidnapping, in a CIA record dated September 5, 1985. A rebel communique states demands and terms in formal language. This one addressed the seizure that held the country's attention.

Inside, the front's official statement on the case is preserved. Its terms framed what any settlement would have to answer. Communiques were the rebels' way of negotiating in public print. They spoke to the government, to the country, and to foreign readers all in the same few formal lines. The file holds their stated position from that September, against which the secret talks and the final release can be measured by any later reader.
cia-0000049001: The extreme left intended to hold a six-day wake in El Salvador's National Cathedral in 1980, and a CIA item from that year preserves the plan. A wake of that length, in the country's chief church, was mourning staged as a show of strength. The item preserves the plan as officials learned of it, in a season when grief and protest had merged.
cia-0000049201: The military pressed El Salvador's minister of defense in 1990 to resolve the Jesuit murder case, and a CIA item records the pressure. Resolving it could mean solving it or burying it, and the files do not always say which was meant by the men applying it. The item survives in the Truth Commission records.
cia-0000049301: The pistols used in insurgent assassinations in El Salvador are catalogued in a CIA item from 1989, kept under the Truth Commission's eye. Weapons were evidence with serial numbers: a pistol tied to one killing could tie a whole network together. The catalogue's dry detail served the most concrete kind of investigation.
cia-0000095001: Redacted comments on deteriorating North Vietnamese-Chinese relations and related claims fill declassified CIA document 0000095001, dated September 5, 1968. The heading marks part of the text as deleted. The brief file centers on worsening ties between two allied governments, preserved as comments rather than a finished estimate, with the deletion noted in the record itself.
cia-0000096501: Progress report on the implementation of Recommendation number two, with implementation misspelled in the original heading, is declassified CIA document 0000096501, dated July 4, 1958. The typo survives in the catalog title. Readers get a later-year installment of the recommendation series, its flawed heading a small honest sign of the record's age.
cia-0000097301: Proposal for Photographic Reconnaissance of Cuba, with reconnaissance run into the next word in the heading, is declassified CIA document 0000097301, dated April 2, 1982. The title proposes aerial photography of the island. Readers get a short declassified proposal record, the spacing flaw in its heading preserved, filed two decades after the earliest Cuba items here.
cia-0000113201: Dated January 1, 1945, with that date marked as an estimate, declassified CIA document 0000113201 lists additional target addresses in Wehrkreis V. Its heading notes pages as received, in a word that breaks off at Recei. Wehrkreis V is a German military district, named in the title itself. The brief record preserves the estimate note and the broken ending as released.
cia-0000119201:
Filed in February 1986, this declassified CIA record concerns a deceased pilot who flew for Air America. The pilot's name was deleted before release, so the record keeps the fact of his death but not his identity. Air America was the airline the agency owned and used for secret flights across Southeast Asia.

Records like this one show the human cost behind the agency's covert air operations. A pilot died in that service, and the paperwork outlived him. Because the name is withheld, the document works less as a biography than as a marker in the agency's own files. It is proof that the loss was noted and kept.
cia-0000122101: A March 1960 CIA report gives the outlook for the Dominican Republic. Trujillo's long dictatorship was entering its final year, though no one could know that yet. The paper forecasts the country's course on the edge of the upheaval that followed his fall. Outlook papers on small Caribbean states reflected a Washington habit of the era: treat each island's politics as a piece of the larger contest with Castro.
cia-0000132201: Situation report 518, from January 1991, covers Saddam talking with CNN reporter Peter Arnett, his surname misspelled in the heading, and Baghdad, the title breaking off. The Iraqi leader used the network as his channel to the West. The report covers the interview. Arnett's broadcasts from Baghdad were a novelty in war reporting, watched in the White House and in Baghdad alike, which is why a sitrep tracked the interview.
cia-0000132501: Communist and Castro influence dominating a Latin American peace congress fills a CIA document dated February 1, 1961. Such congresses gave communist parties a respectable stage across the region. Havana worked the peace movement hard as a channel for its own message. The short document covers the congress and the influence the agency saw behind it, in the last weeks before the Bay of Pigs invasion changed the contest.
cia-0000132601: Seven countries abstaining on a Cuban resolution fill item 6 of the CIA's Latin America series. The item is dated August 4, 1960. The headline breaks off at the name of the committee hearing the matter. Abstention was how many governments ducked the Cuba question in public votes that year. The short item reports the vote and the lineup behind it.
cia-0000135601: Filed in the CIA's declassified 2506 Brigade papers, this Spanish-language document is dated 2 November 1960. Brigade 2506 was the force of Cuban exiles the agency trained for a landing in Cuba, which came at the Bay of Pigs in April 1961. The catalog title names no subject, author, or unit for this item, so its contents cannot be summarized from the record alone. It survives in the original Spanish, released through the CIA Reading Room, as one piece of the brigade's own paperwork from its training months.
cia-0000135701: Dated 2 January 1961, this Spanish text is another of the 2506 Brigade records carrying that date. Brigade 2506 was the force of Cuban exiles that the CIA landed at the Bay of Pigs that April. In January it was still an unnamed unit in training. The catalog names no subject for this document. Kept in its original Spanish, it forms part of the brigade's declassified paperwork from the operation's last winter.
cia-0000135801: A declassified CIA document dated 2 August 1953 turns to assassins named by Guatemala to kill Calligeris, a threat reported back in the summer of 1953. All of it feeds into PBSUCCESS, the agency operation against the Arbenz government in the months before the June 1954 coup. The paper trail here is small but direct, a single piece of the huge file the operation left behind.
cia-0000135901: One declassified report from the CIA files, dated about April 1954, covers an operational report from the field, with the name of its author deleted in the heading. The paper sits inside the CIA drive against President Arbenz, run under the code name PBSUCCESS and crowned by the June 1954 coup. Later books on the coup rest on stacks of paper exactly like this, dated, coded, and only partly opened.
cia-0000136001: The CIA cable of 5 February 1954 is about the first results of a debriefing of CADICK and ONTRICH, and it survives in declassified form. Traffic like this ran the field side of PBSUCCESS, the secret CIA effort against the Arbenz government in Guatemala. Students of the 1954 coup use such records to check later accounts against what was written at the time.
cia-0000136101: The CIA situation report from 2 March 1954 deals with the Lincoln weekly situation report for 19 to 26 April, filed under a March date, in a file now declassified. In these files Lincoln names the field station of PBSUCCESS, the covert CIA plan to topple President Arbenz of Guatemala. The heading alone tells a reader the topic, the channel, and the moment, even where names stay deleted.
cia-0000136201: The CIA press file of 4 May 1954 is about the Guatemalan daily Tribuna Popular for the first six days of June, and it survives in declassified form. The paper sits inside the CIA drive against President Arbenz, run under the code name PBSUCCESS and crowned by the June 1954 coup. Its worth is in the detail it pins down, one dated piece of a covert war fought largely on paper.
cia-0000136301: STORAX's concern with military planning and tactics is the subject of this June 1954 LINCOLN cable from the PBSUCCESS files. The station questions whether a proposed trip is necessary at all, and insists that if it happens, a military man, not a civilian, should go. Dunbar is named the best candidate, given his army background and knowledge of the operation, and could be spared for two days. It is a small staffing argument inside a covert war.
cia-0000136401: Silence is hurting CALLIGERIS, headquarters tells LINCOLN in this January 1954 cable. It urges a clear course for his travel. He should go soonest via Havana. He should use his present papers. There he can give approved speech lines to the press. He can also use radio and other publicity. When those outlets run out, he should return via New Orleans. Then he should vanish from public view. Funds are approved for the trip.
cia-0000137001: An early move might be counterproductive, this June 1954 cable indicates. The possible move would be against the Arbenz regime. Somoza would presumably make it. Remon would presumably acquiesce. The surviving text is very fragmentary. A summary line is almost all that remains. Another component's position is noted only in part. Little more can honestly be recovered. The cable still records a real debate. Headquarters weighed whether allied dictators striking early would hurt the plan.
cia-0000140401: Four questions define the Bluebird program in this January 1952 paper. Bluebird was the forerunner of Artichoke and MKULTRA. Can true facts be got from willing or unwilling people? Can agency staff be trained to resist outside pressure? Can control of a person's future acts be obtained? Can outside control of agency personnel be prevented? Bluebird believes the first can be answered yes. Interrogation and hypnosis techniques support that belief. It is not fully pleased with results to date.
cia-03139101:
A memorandum for the Director, dated 3 November 1962, reconstructs his briefings of the National Security Council's Executive Committee during the Cuban missile crisis. Day by day, from 23 October, it lists what he told the group. Construction at the missile sites was continuing. Twenty-two Soviet ships were en route to Cuba. Fifteen of them soon turned back. Lundahl briefed on photographs, and two men were sent to help Ambassador Stevenson in New York.

Later entries track the crisis turning. Sites at San Cristobal and Sagua la Grande appeared fully operational by 27 October. Soviet forces had completed alert measures without significant deployments. Secure scrambler communications between Cuba and the USSR were established on 28 October. Cuban forces were ordered not to fire unless attacked. The Director also warned that press stories based on special intelligence had to be prevented.
cia-06928801:
Intelligence Report titled Shanghai, number CIA/BGI GR 72-7 and dated January 1972, is marked Confidential with No Foreign Dissem. It is a Directorate of Intelligence study of the city. Its introduction traces how Shanghai grew on the Yangtze trade.

The report states Shanghai's hinterland was the 750,000 square miles of the Yangtze Basin, holding perhaps half of China's population. Foreign access came with the 1842 Treaty of Nanking, which ended the Opium War and opened five ports to trade. British, European, American, and later Japanese traders then settled outside Chinese law, it states. In 1843 the first British consul arranged a 43-acre site near the meeting of two rivers. Later sections cover climate, with 45 inches of yearly rain falling mostly from March to October, and points of interest such as the Bund and Nanking Road.
cleopatra-volume-01:
Volume 1 of Cleopatra begins the best known Alexandria novel by Georg Ebers, translated from the German by Mary J Safford. Ebers opens with a preface defending his queen against hostile Roman writers. He argues that poets serving Rome painted Cleopatra unfairly because she had humbled Caesar and Antony, two of Rome's greatest men.

Inside the story, Alexandria glitters with learning, wealth, and court ceremony as Antony returns to the queen. Young Barine, from a family of scholars, draws royal attention she does not want. Dion, her lover, must weigh safety against honor. Ebers mixes documented history, including Plutarch, with invented households, so readers meet the famous lovers through the eyes of ordinary Alexandrians caught in their path.
coniston-volume-01:
Winston Churchill, the American novelist, opens Coniston with a warning that his first love story ends in sorrow. Jackson has just reached the White House as this New Hampshire tale begins. Churchill calls the age the Boss-Era, when men found cracks in the Constitution and stole the people's chestnuts. A longer, happier love story, he promises, waits further on.

Coniston Mountain and Coniston Water frame the valley where Cynthia Ware is born. Towns Brampton and Harwich fight for the river's power below the notch. Boss Jethro Bass rises through this landscape, gathering votes, debts, and silence into one man's hands. The first love story belongs to Cynthia's parents and closes, as promised, without joy. Around it, Churchill builds his case that democracy fails when virtue sleeps and bosses wake. Readers starting the novel get place, politics, and tragedy laid out, in period prose and New England dialect.
constitution-mongolia-2001:
Mongolia adopted this constitution in 1992, as communist rule ended, and the hosted text carries changes through 2001. Chapter one covers sovereignty. Mongolia is a single republic, and Mongolian is the official language. Chapter two protects human rights and freedoms in detail, from life and free speech to property, schooling, and a healthy environment.

A president, chosen by direct vote, heads the state and can veto laws. A prime minister leads the government and holds most day-to-day power. The State Great Khural, a single chamber, makes the laws. Later chapters cover the courts, a Constitutional Court called the Tsets, local rule, and finance. At seventy articles the text is compact. Later changes in 2019 shifted more power to the prime minister.
cumner-s-son-and-other-south-sea-folk-vo:
Cumner's Son and Other South Sea Folk, Volume 1, by Gilbert Parker, gives its whole space to the title tale. Parker's contents page for the five volume set shows what surrounds it elsewhere, Australian and Pacific stories in bulk, but this first volume stands on Cumner's Son alone. The tale is set in a South Seas world of traders, officials, and island peoples.

Cumner is an old official whose authority in the islands is personal rather than legal, and his son inherits both the influence and its enemies. Native politics, white traders' schemes, and the slow machinery of empire meet in one harbor. Parker writes colonial fiction from inside the administration's veranda. Loyalty to old chiefs matters there. New regulations do not.
cushing-zuni-folk-tales-1901:
Frank Hamilton Cushing lived at Zuni Pueblo in New Mexico for years in the 1880s. He learned the language and joined pueblo life to a degree no outsider had before. His 1901 book retells the folk tales he heard there, gathered from Zuni storytellers.

Coyote appears again and again, greedy, foolish, and impossible to kill. He teaches lessons by failing at them. Other tales tell of the twin war gods and of the people's emergence from the underworld into this world. Cushing shaped the stories for English readers while keeping their humor and strangeness. The book is a beloved early window into Zuni imagination.
dedekind-essays-theory-numbers-beman-190:
Richard Dedekind gave the real numbers a rigorous base in two essays, Englished by Wooster Woodruff Beman in 1901. The first essay treats continuity and irrational numbers. Its method, the Dedekind cut, splits the rationals into two classes to define each irrational. The second essay asks the nature and meaning of numbers themselves.

Dedekind builds the natural numbers from sets and mappings, step by careful step. His aim was to free arithmetic from vague appeals to intuition. The essays are short, dense, and exact. Mathematicians still teach the cut that bears his name. Readers who work through them see modern rigor being born. Few pages changed math so much.
defoe-true-born-englishman-1701:
Daniel Defoe published The True-Born Englishman in 1701, a bestselling verse satire for William III. The poem defends the Dutch-born king against xenophobic attacks on his foreign birth and court in England. Its famous line holds that the English are really all foreigners themselves in blood and stock.
